Though their beneficial effects, however, have been in this respect accidental, they have not upon that account been less real.
p61.zh: 其中一些条例往往提高美国的木材价值,从而便利土地的清理,但这种倾向也许并没有得到立法机构的打算或理解。 然而,虽然它们的有利影响是偶然的,但从这个角度讲,它们并非不太真实。

p62.original: The most perfect freedom of trade is permitted between the British colonies of America and the West Indies, both in the enumerated and in the non-enumerated commodities Those colonies are now become so populous and thriving, that each of them finds in some of the others a great and extensive market for every part of its produce. All of them taken together, they make a great internal market for the produce of one another.
p62.zh: 美国和西印度群岛的英属殖民地之间允许最完美的贸易自由,无论是在列举的商品中还是在未加工的商品中,这些殖民地现在都变得如此人口众多和兴旺,在另一些殖民地中,每一个殖民地都为其农产品的每一个部分找到一个大而广泛的市场。将它们结合在一起,它们为彼此的产物创造了一个巨大的内部市场.

p63.original: The liberality of England, however, towards the trade of her colonies, has been confined chiefly to what concerns the market for their produce, either in its rude state, or in what may be called the very first stage of manufacture. The more advanced or more refined manufactures, even of the colony produce, the merchants and manufacturers of Great Britain chuse to reserve to themselves, and have prevailed upon the legislature to prevent their establishment in the colonies, sometimes by high duties, and sometimes by absolute prohibitions.
p63.zh: 然而,英格兰对其殖民地贸易的自由化主要局限于与其产品市场有关的方面,无论是在粗鲁的状态下,还是在可能被称为制造的第一阶段。更先进或更精细的制造品,甚至殖民地的产物,大不列颠的商人和制造商都保留给自己,并且已经压倒立法机关阻止他们在殖民地的建立,有时是高职,有时是绝对禁止.

p64.original: While, for example, Muscovado sugars from the British plantations pay, upon importation, only 6s:4d. the hundred weight, white sugars pay £1:1:1; and refined, either double or single, in loaves, £4:2:5 8/20ths. When those high duties were imposed, Great Britain was the sole, and she still continues to be, the principal market, to which the sugars of the British colonies could be exported. They amounted, therefore, to a prohibition, at first of claying or refining sugar for any foreign market, and at present of claying or refining it for the market which takes off, perhaps, more than nine-tenths of the whole produce. The manufacture of claying or refining sugar, accordingly, though it has flourished in all the sugar colonies of France, has been little cultivated in any of those of England, except for the market of the colonies themselves. While Grenada was in the hands of the French, there was a refinery of sugar, by claying, at least upon almost every plantation. Since it fell into those of the English, almost all works of this kind have been given up; and there are at present (October 1773), I am assured, not above two or three remaining in the island. At present, however, by an indulgence of the custom-house, clayed or refined sugar, if reduced from loaves into powder, is commonly imported as Muscovado.
p64.zh: 例如,英国种植园的穆斯科瓦多糖在进口时只支付6:4d. 百重,白糖支付1:1英镑;精制,双倍或单倍,以树脂支付4:2:58/20英镑.征收这些高额关税时,大不列颠是唯一的,她仍然是主要市场,英国殖民地的糖可以出口到那里. 因此,它们相当于禁止首先为任何外国市场粘土或炼制糖,目前禁止为可能起飞的全产的九分之十以上的市场粘土或炼制糖。 因此,粘土或炼糖的制造虽然在法国所有的糖殖民地都蓬勃发展,但在英格兰的任何一个殖民地,除了殖民地本身的市场之外,都很少种植.格林纳达在法国人手中时,至少在每个种植园都有糖的炼油厂。 由于属于英语作品,几乎所有这类作品都被放弃了;目前(1773年10月),我确信,岛上还剩下两三部作品。 然而,目前,由于对定制房的放任,粘土或精制糖如果从薄饼中减成粉末,通常会作为Muscovado进口。

p65.original: While Great Britain encourages in America the manufacturing of pig and bar iron, by exempting them from duties to which the like commodities are subject when imported from any other country, she imposes an absolute prohibition upon the erection of steel furnaces and slit-mills in any of her American plantations. She will not suffer her colonies to work in those more refined manufactures, even for their own consumption; but insists upon their purchasing of her merchants and manufacturers all goods of this kind which they have occasion for.
p65.zh: 虽然英国鼓励美国生产猪和巴铁,但英国免除了从其他国家进口类似商品的关税,绝对禁止在其任何美国种植园安装钢炉和滑轮机。 她的殖民地不会在那些更精细的制成品中工作,即使这些制成品自己消费;但坚持要求这些制成品购买她商家和制造商所有他们有机会购买的这种商品。

p66.original: She prohibits the exportation from one province to another by water, and even the carriage by land upon horseback, or in a cart, of hats, of wools, and woollen goods, of the produce of America; a regulation which effectually prevents the establishment of any manufacture of such commodities for distant sale, and confines the industry of her colonists in this way to such coarse and household manufactures as a private family commonly makes for its own use, or for that of some of its neighbours in the same province.
p66.zh: 她禁止从一个省份通过水出口到另一个省份,甚至禁止用马背或马车从陆路运输美国农产品的帽子、羊毛和羊毛制品;这项条例实际上阻止了制造任何供远期销售的此类商品,并将殖民者以这种方式从事的工业限于私人家庭通常为其自身或同一省份的一些邻国制造的粗糙和家用产品。

p67.original: To prohibit a great people, however, from making all that they can of every part of their own produce, or from employing their stock and industry in the way that they judge most advantageous to themselves, is a manifest violation of the most sacred rights of mankind. Unjust, however, as such prohibitions may be, they have not hitherto been very hurtful to the colonies. Land is still so cheap, and, consequently, labour so dear among them, that they can import from the mother country almost all the more refined or more advanced manufactures cheaper than they could make them for themselves. Though they had not, therefore, been prohibited from establishing such manufactures, yet, in their present state of improvement, a regard to their own interest would probably have prevented them from doing so. In their present state of improvement, those prohibitions, perhaps, without cramping their industry, or restraining it from any employment to which it would have gone of its own accord, are only impertinent badges of slavery imposed upon them, without any sufficient reason, by the groundless jealousy of the merchants and manufacturers of the mother country. In a more advanced state, they might be really oppressive and insupportable.
p67.zh: 然而,禁止一个伟大的民族尽其所能生产自己的每一部分产品,或以他们认为自己最有利的方式利用自己的股票和工业,是对人类最神圣权利的公然侵犯。 然而,这种禁令可能不合理,但迄今为止对殖民地并没有造成很大伤害。土地仍然如此便宜,因此,他们中十分珍贵的劳动力,因此他们可以从祖国进口几乎所有更精炼或更先进的制成品,比他们自己能做的便宜。 因此,虽然它们没有被禁止建立这种制造,但是,在目前改进的状态下,考虑到它们自己的利益,它们很可能无法这样做。 这些禁令在目前有所改善的情况下,也许在不压缩其产业或限制其从事任何本可以自行从事的工作的情况下,只是毫无理由地由母国商人和制造商无端嫉妒而强加给他们的奴役的不必要徽章。在一个更先进的状态下,他们可能真的压迫和不支持.

p68.original: Great Britain, too, as she confines to her own market some of the most important productions of the colonies, so, in compensation, she gives to some of them an advantage in that market, sometimes by imposing higher duties upon the like productions when imported from other countries, and sometimes by giving bounties upon their importation from the colonies. In the first way, she gives an advantage in the home market to the sugar, tobacco, and iron of her own colonies; and, in the second, to their raw silk, to their hemp and flax, to their indigo, to their naval stores, and to their building timber. This second way of encouraging the colony produce, by bounties upon importation, is, so far as I have been able to learn, peculiar to Great Britain: the first is not. Portugal does not content herself with imposing higher duties upon the importation of tobacco from any other country, but prohibits it under the severest penalties.
p68.zh: 大不列颠也将殖民地的一些最重要的产品限制在自己的市场,因此,作为补偿,她在市场上给予其中一些人一种优势,有时从其他国家进口时对类似产品征收更高的关税,有时从殖民地进口时给予好处。 首先,她在家中市场中给自己的聚居地的糖,烟草,铁提供了优势;其次,给她们生的丝绸,他们的大麻和麻油,他们的indigo,他们的海军商店,以及他们的建筑木材. 这种鼓励殖民地生产的第二种方式,在进口时得到好处,就我所知,是大不列颠独有的:第一种不是。 葡萄牙不满足于对从任何其他国家进口烟草规定更高的关税,而是以最严厉的惩罚禁止进口烟草。

p69.original: With regard to the importation of goods from Europe, England has likewise dealt more liberally with her colonies than any other nation.
p69.zh: 关于从欧洲进口货物的问题,英格兰也比任何其他国家更自由地对待其殖民地。

p70.original: Great Britain allows a part, almost always the half, generally a larger portion, and sometimes the whole, of the duty which is paid upon the importation of foreign goods, to be drawn back upon their exportation to any foreign country. No independent foreign country, it was easy to foresee, would receive them, if they came to it loaded with the heavy duties to which almost all foreign goods are subjected on their importation into Great Britain. Unless, therefore, some part of those duties was drawn back upon exportation, there was an end of the carrying trade; a trade so much favoured by the mercantile system.
p70.zh: 大不列颠允许在出口到任何外国后收回进口外国货物时所应支付义务的一部分,几乎总是一半,一般是更大一部分,有时是全部。任何独立的外国,只要它们来到英国时都承担着几乎所有外国货物进口到大不列颠时所必须承担的沉重义务,就很容易预见到它们会接收到它们。 因此,除非这些关税的一部分在出口后被收回,否则承载贸易即告结束;这种贸易非常受商贸制度所青睐。

p71.original: Our colonies, however, are by no means independent foreign countries; and Great Britain having assumed to herself the exclusive right of supplying them with all goods from Europe, might have forced them (in the same manner as other countries have done their colonies) to receive such goods loaded with all the same duties which they paid in the mother country. But, on the contrary, till 1763, the same drawbacks were paid upon the exportation of the greater part of foreign goods to our colonies, as to any independent foreign country. In 1763, indeed, by the 4th of Geo. III. c. 15, this indulgence was a good deal abated, and it was enacted, "That no part of the duty called the old subsidy should be drawn back for any goods of the growth, production, or manufacture of Europe or the East Indies, which should be exported from this kingdom to any British colony or plantation in America; wines, white calicoes, and muslins, excepted." Before this law, many different sorts of foreign goods might have been bought cheaper in the plantations than in the mother country, and some may still.
p71.zh: 然而,我们的殖民地绝不是独立的外国;大不列颠本身拥有向它们供应来自欧洲的所有货物的专有权利,可能迫使它们(以其他国家完成殖民地的方式)接受这些货物,这些货物上载了它们在母国支付的所有相同义务。 但与此相反,直到1763年,向我国殖民地出口大部分外国货物,对任何独立的外国,都造成了同样的损失。1763年,确实,由"地"4号. 三. C. 组织事项15,这种宽大待遇得到了很好的缓解,并且颁布,"任何被称为旧补贴的关税部分都不应该被收回来用于任何欧洲或东印度群岛的成长,生产或制造商品,这些商品应该从本王国出口到美国的任何英国殖民地或种植园;葡萄酒,白卡利科酒,和木斯林酒,除了此之外". 在这部法律之前,许多不同的外国商品在种植园中被买得比在祖国更便宜,有些可能还可能仍然.

p72.original: Of the greater part of the regulations concerning the colony trade, the merchants who carry it on, it must be observed, have been the principal advisers. We must not wonder, therefore, if, in a great part of them, their interest has been more considered than either that of the colonies or that of the mother country. In their exclusive privilege of supplying the colonies with all the goods which they wanted from Europe, and of purchasing all such parts of their surplus produce as could not interfere with any of the trades which they themselves carried on at home, the interest of the colonies was sacrificed to the interest of those merchants. In allowing the same drawbacks upon the re-exportation of the greater part of European and East India goods to the colonies, as upon their re-exportation to any independent country, the interest of the mother country was sacrificed to it, even according to the mercantile ideas of that interest. It was for the interest of the merchants to pay as little as possible for the foreign goods which they sent to the colonies, and, consequently, to get back as much as possible of the duties which they advanced upon their importation into Great Britain. They might thereby be enabled to sell in the colonies, either the same quantity of goods with a greater profit, or a greater quantity with the same profit, and, consequently, to gain something either in the one way or the other. It was likewise for the interest of the colonies to get all such goods as cheap, and in as great abundance as possible. But this might not always be for the interest of the mother country. She might frequently suffer, both in her revenue, by giving back a great part of the duties which had been paid upon the importation of such goods; and in her manufactures, by being undersold in the colony market, in consequence of the easy terms upon which foreign manufactures could be carried thither by means of those drawbacks. The progress of the linen manufacture of Great Britain, it is commonly said, has been a good deal retarded by the drawbacks upon the re-exportation of German linen to the American colonies.
p72.zh: 在关于殖民地贸易的大部分条例中,必须注意的是,进行这种贸易的商人是主要的顾问。 因此,我们决不能怀疑,在他们中的大部分国家,他们的利益是否比殖民地的利益或祖国的利益受到更多的考虑。殖民地拥有从欧洲向它们供应一切货物,购买其剩余产品的所有部分的专属特权,而这些部分不能干涉它们自己在国内进行的任何贸易,因此,殖民地的利益被牺牲给这些商人的利益。 由于允许将大部分欧洲和东印度货物再出口到殖民地,如同再出口到任何独立国家一样,母国的利益被牺牲,即使根据这种利益的商业想法也是如此。商人们的利益在于尽可能少地支付他们寄往殖民地的外国货物,从而尽可能地收回他们进口到大不列颠时所增加的关税。 因此,它们可以在殖民地出售相同数量的货物,利润较高,或利润相同,从而以某种方式获得某种利益。 同样,为了殖民地的利益,应尽量以廉价和丰厚的价格获得所有这些货物。 但这可能并不总是符合祖国的利益。 她的收入经常会受到影响,因为她交还了进口这些货物时所支付的大部分关税;在她的制成品中,由于外国制成品很容易通过这些弊端进行运输,因此在殖民地市场上被低价出售。通常说,大不列颠亚麻布制造的进展由于德国亚麻布再出口到美洲殖民地的缺点而受到了很大的阻碍。

p73.original: But though the policy of Great Britain, with regard to the trade of her colonies, has been dictated by the same mercantile spirit as that of other nations, it has, however, upon the whole, been less illiberal and oppressive than that of any of them.
p73.zh: 但是,虽然大不列颠关于殖民地贸易的政策是与其他国家一样的商贸精神所决定的,但总的来说,这种政策比任何一个国家的不自由和压迫性都低。

p74.original: In every thing except their foreign trade, the liberty of the English colonists to manage their own affairs their own way, is complete. It is in every respect equal to that of their fellow-citizens at home, and is secured in the same manner, by an assembly of the representatives of the people, who claim the sole right of imposing taxes for the support of the colony government. The authority of this assembly overawes the executive power; and neither the meanest nor the most obnoxious colonist, as long as he obeys the law, has any thing to fear from the resentment, either of the governor, or of any other civil or military officer in the province. The colony assemblies, though, like the house of commons in England, they are not always a very equal representation of the people, yet they approach more nearly to that character; and as the executive power either has not the means to corrupt them, or, on account of the support which it receives from the mother country, is not under the necessity of doing so, they are, perhaps, in general more influenced by the inclinations of their constituents. The councils, which, in the colony legislatures, correspond to the house of lords in Great Britain, are not composed of a hereditary nobility. In some of the colonies, as in three of the governments of New England, those councils are not appointed by the king, but chosen by the representatives of the people. In none of the English colonies is there any hereditary nobility. In all of them, indeed, as in all other free countries, the descendant of an old colony family is more respected than an upstart of equal merit and fortune; but he is only more respected, and he has no privileges by which he can be troublesome to his neighbours. Before the commencement of the present disturbances, the colony assemblies had not only the legislative, but a part of the executive power. In Connecticut and Rhode Island, they elected the governor. In the other colonies, they appointed the revenue officers, who collected the taxes imposed by those respective assemblies, to whom those officers were immediately responsible. There is more equality, therefore, among the English colonists than among the inhabitants of the mother country. Their manners are more re publican; and their governments, those of three of the provinces of New England in particular, have hitherto been more republican too.
p74.zh: 除了对外贸易之外,英国殖民者管理自己事务的自由是完全的。 它在各个方面都与本国同胞平等,并以同样的方式,由人民代表大会确保,人民代表声称,他们有唯一的权利为殖民地政府提供支助而征税。本届议会的权威管理着行政权力;最卑劣的殖民者,只要服从法律,就没有什么可害怕的,无论是省长还是省内任何其他文职或军事官员的怨恨.殖民地议会,虽然与英国的公社一样,并不总是人民享有非常平等的代表性,但更接近于这种特性;由于行政权力没有手段来腐蚀他们,或者由于它从祖国得到的支持,因此没有必要这样做,因此,他们可能普遍受到其选民倾向的影响。 在殖民地立法机关中,议会与大不列颠的领主府相对应,不由世袭贵族组成.在一些殖民地中,如在新英格兰的3个政府中,这些议会不是由国王任命的,而是由人民代表选择的. 在英国殖民地中,没有哪个是世袭贵族. 实际上,在所有这些国家中,同其他所有的自由国家一样,一个旧殖民地家庭的后裔比起平等功绩和财富的起步,更加受到尊重;但他只是受到更多的尊重,他没有特权可以给邻居带来麻烦。 在目前的动乱开始之前,殖民地议会不仅拥有立法权,而且还拥有部分行政权力。 在康涅狄格州和罗德岛州,他们选出了州长. 在其他殖民地,他们任命了税务官员,负责征收这些议会规定的税款,这些官员立即对这些官员负责。 因此,在英国殖民者中,比在祖国的居民中,平等程度更高。 他们的礼仪更是公开;他们的政府,特别是新英格兰三个省的政府,至今也更加共和.

p75.original: The absolute governments of Spain, Portugal, and France, on the contrary, take place in their colonies; and the discretionary powers which such governments commonly delegate to all their inferior officers are, on account of the great distance, naturally exercised there with more than ordinary violence. Under all absolute governments, there is more liberty in the capital than in any other part of the country. The sovereign himself can never have either interest or inclination to pervert the order of justice, or to oppress the great body of the people. In the capital, his presence overawes, more or less, all his inferior officers, who, in the remoter provinces, from whence the complaints of the people are less likely to reach him, can exercise their tyranny with much more safety. But the European colonies in America are more remote than the most distant provinces of the greatest empires which had ever been known before. The government of the English colonies is, perhaps, the only one which, since the world began, could give perfect security to the inhabitants of so very distant a province. The administration of the French colonies, however, has always been conducted with much more gentleness and moderation than that of the Spanish and Portuguese. This superiority of conduct is suitable both to the character of the French nation, and to what forms the character of every nation, the nature of their government, which, though arbitrary and violent in comparison with that of Great Britain, is legal and free in comparison with those of Spain and Portugal.
p75.zh: 相反,西班牙、葡萄牙和法国的绝对政府是在他们的殖民地;由于距离遥远,这些政府通常赋予所有低级军官的酌处权自然是用比普通暴力更严重的暴力行使的。在所有绝对政府之下,首都的自由比国内任何其他地区都多。主权者本身永远不能有利益或倾向扭曲正义秩序,或压迫人民的伟大身体。 在首都,他的存在或多或少地监督着他所有低级军官,他们在较偏远的省份,从人们的抱怨中不太可能到达他那里,他们可以更加安全地行使他们的暴政. 但美洲的欧洲殖民地比以前最伟大的帝国中最遥远的省份要远.英国殖民地政府也许是唯一一个 自世界开始以来 能为如此遥远省份的居民提供 完全安全的人 然而,法国殖民地的管理总是比西班牙人和葡萄牙人要温和和温和得多。行为的这种优越性既适合法国民族的特性,也适合每个国家的特性、其政府的性质,虽然与大不列颠相比是任意的和暴力的,但与西班牙和葡萄牙相比是合法和自由的。

p76.original: It is in the progress of the North American colonies, however, that the superiority of the English policy chiefly appears. The progress of the sugar colonies of France has been at least equal, perhaps superior, to that of the greater part of those of England; and yet the sugar colonies of England enjoy a free government, nearly of the same kind with that which takes place in her colonies of North America. But the sugar colonies of France are not discouraged, like those of England, from refining their own sugar; and what is still of greater importance, the genius of their government naturally introduces a better management of their negro slaves.
p76.zh: 然而,正是在北美殖民地的进步中,英国政策的优越性主要显现出来. 法国的糖殖民地的进步至少与英国大部分的相比是平等的,或许是优越的;然而英格兰的糖殖民地却享有自由政府,几乎与她在北美殖民地中发生的类似. 但是,法国的糖殖民地并没有像英国的殖民地那样劝阻他们改良自己的糖;而那些仍然更重要的,他们的政府的天才自然地引入了对其黑人奴隶的更好的管理.

p77.original: In all European colonies, the culture of the sugar-cane is carried on by negro slaves. The constitution of those who have been born in the temperate climate of Europe could not, it is supposed, support the labour of digging the ground under the burning sun of the West Indies; and the culture of the sugar-cane, as it is managed at present, is all hand labour; though, in the opinion of many, the drill plough might be introduced into it with great advantage. But, as the profit and success of the cultivation which is carried on by means of cattle, depend very much upon the good management of those cattle; so the profit and success of that which is carried on by slaves must depend equally upon the good management of those slaves; and in the good management of their slaves the French planters, I think it is generally allowed, are superior to the English. The law, so far as it gives some weak protection to the slave against the violence of his master, is likely to be better executed in a colony where the government is in a great measure arbitrary, than in one where it is altogether free. In ever country where the unfortunate law of slavery is established, the magistrate, when he protects the slave, intermeddles in some measure in the management of the private property of the master; and, in a free country, where the master is, perhaps, either a member of the colony assembly, or an elector of such a member, he dares not do this but with the greatest caution and circumspection. The respect which he is obliged to pay to the master, renders it more difficult for him to protect the slave. But in a country where the government is in a great measure arbitrary, where it is usual for the magistrate to intermeddle even in the management of the private property of individuals, and to send them, perhaps, a lettre de cachet, if they do not manage it according to his liking, it is much easier for him to give some protection to the slave; and common humanity naturally disposes him to do so. The protection of the magistrate renders the slave less contemptible in the eyes of his master, who is thereby induced to consider him with more regard, and to treat him with more gentleness. Gentle usage renders the slave not only more faithful, but more intelligent, and, therefore, upon a double account, more useful. He approaches more to the condition of a free servant, and may possess some degree of integrity and attachment to his master's interest; virtues which frequently belong to free servants, but which never can belong to a slave, who is treated as slaves commonly are in countries where the master is perfectly free and secure.
p77.zh: 在所有欧洲殖民地中,甘蔗文化由黑人奴隶延续.生于欧洲温带气候下的人的宪法,应该不能支持在西印度群岛燃烧的太阳下挖地的劳动;而目前管理着的甘蔗文化,都是手工劳动;不过,许多人认为钻犁可能以极大的优势引入其中. 但是,由于靠牛进行耕作的利润和成功,在很大程度上取决于这些牛的良好管理;因此奴隶进行耕作的利润和成功必须同样取决于这些奴隶的良好管理;在他们的奴隶的良好管理中,我认为法国的种植者一般是允许的,比英国人优越.法律,只要对奴隶提供一些薄弱的保护,使其免受主人的暴力,那么在政府在很大程度上是任意的殖民地里,比在完全自由的殖民地里,执行得更好。 在任何建立奴隶制这一不幸法律的国家,地方法官在保护奴隶时,在某种程度上干预主人的私有财产的管理;在自由的国家,主人或许是殖民地大会的成员,或这种成员的选举人,他不敢这样做,而是极其谨慎和谨慎。 他有义务尊重主人,使他更难保护奴隶。 但是在一个政府极专横的国家里,地方官通常甚至干涉个人私有财产的管理,并派他们,也许,一个闲置的缓存,如果他们不按照他的喜好管理,那么他给奴隶一些保护就容易多了;而共同的人性自然地支配他这样做.地方官的保护使得奴隶在主人的眼里不那么可鄙,因此他被诱使更以更尊重的态度看待他,更温柔地对待他.温柔的用法不仅使奴隶更加忠心,而且更加聪明,因此,在双重考虑下,也更加有用。 他更接近自由仆人的条件,可能具有某种程度的正直和对主人利益的依恋;美德常常属于自由仆人,但永远不能属于奴隶,一般被作为奴隶对待的奴隶,是在主人完全自由和安全的国家.

p78.original: That the condition of a slave is better under an arbitrary than under a free government, is, I believe, supported by the history of all ages and nations. In the Roman history, the first time we read of the magistrate interposing to protect the slave from the violence of his master, is under the emperors. When Vidius Pollio, in the presence of Augustus, ordered one of his slaves, who had committed a slight fault, to be cut into pieces and thrown into his fish-pond, in order to feed his fishes, the emperor commanded him, with indignation, to emancipate immediately, not only that slave, but all the others that belonged to him. Under the republic no magistrate could have had authority enough to protect the slave, much less to punish the master.
p78.zh: 我认为,奴隶的条件在任意统治下比在自由政府下好,这得到了所有年龄和国家的历史的支持。在罗马史上,第一次读到地方官介入保护奴隶免受主人暴力侵犯,是在皇帝之下. 当维迪乌斯·波列奥在奥古斯都面前命令他的一位奴隶,他犯了轻微的过失,为了喂养他的鱼而被切成碎块,扔进他的鱼蓬中,皇帝愤慨地命令他立即解放,不仅是那个奴隶,还有属于他的所有其他奴隶. 在共和国之下,没有地方法官有足够权力保护奴隶,更不能惩罚主人。

p79.original: The stock, it is to be observed, which has improved the sugar colonies of France, particularly the great colony of St Domingo, has been raised almost entirely from the gradual improvement and cultivation of those colonies. It has been almost altogether the produce of the soil and of the industry of the colonists, or, what comes to the same thing, the price of that produce, gradually accumulated by good management, and employed in raising a still greater produce. But the stock which has improved and cultivated the sugar colonies of England, has, a great part of it, been sent out from England, and has by no means been altogether the produce of the soil and industry of the colonists. The prosperity of the English sugar colonies has been in a great measure owing to the great riches of England, of which a part has overflowed, if one may say so, upon these colonies. But the prosperity of the sugar colonies of France has been entirely owing to the good conduct of the colonists, which must therefore have had some superiority over that of the English; and this superiority has been remarked in nothing so much as in the good management of their slaves.
p79.zh: 需要指出的是,这些种群改善了法国的糖类殖民地,特别是圣多明各大殖民地,几乎全部是由这些殖民地的逐步改善和种植而来。 它几乎完全是殖民者的土壤和工业的产物,或者说,同样的事情是,这种产物的价格,通过良好的管理逐渐积累,并用于养殖更大的产物。 但是,已经改善和种植了英格兰的糖殖民地的种群,其中很大一部分是从英国运出,绝不完全是殖民者的土壤和工业的产物。英国糖业殖民地的繁荣在很大程度上是由于英国的巨大财富,如果有人这么说的话,其中的一部分已经溢出在这些殖民地上。 但是,法国的糖殖民地的繁荣完全是由于殖民者的良好行为,因此,他们一定比英国人有一定优势;这种优越性在对奴隶的妥善管理中却一无所获.

p80.original: Such have been the general outlines of the policy of the different European nations with regard to their colonies.
p80.zh: 这就是不同欧洲国家对其殖民地政策的总纲。

p81.original: The policy of Europe, therefore, has very little to boast of, either in the original establishment, or, so far as concerns their internal government, in the subsequent prosperity of the colonies of America.
p81.zh: 因此,欧洲的政策几乎没有什么可夸耀的,无论是在最初的建立中,还是就其内部政府而言,在后来美国殖民地的繁荣中。

p82.original: Folly and injustice seem to have been the principles which presided over and directed the first project of establishing those colonies; the folly of hunting after gold and silver mines, and the injustice of coveting the possession of a country whose harmless natives, far from having ever injured the people of Europe, had received the first adventurers with every mark of kindness and hospitality.
p82.zh: 愚昧和不公正似乎是主持和指导建立这些殖民地的第一个项目的原则;在金银矿后进行狩猎的愚蠢行为;以及贪婪拥有一个国家的不公正行为,这个国家的无辜原住民远未伤害过欧洲人民,却得到了第一任冒险家的恩惠和款待。

p83.original: The adventurers, indeed, who formed some of the latter establishments, joined to the chimerical project of finding gold and silver mines, other motives more reasonable and more laudable; but even these motives do very little honour to the policy of Europe.
p83.zh: 冒险者,的确,他们组成了后一类机构,他们加入了寻找金银矿的奇异项目,其他动机更合理,更值得称赞;但即使这些动机也很少为欧洲的政策带来任何荣誉。

p84.original: The English puritans, restrained at home, fled for freedom to America, and established there the four governments of New England. The English catholics, treated with much greater injustice, established that of Maryland; the quakers, that of Pennsylvania. The Portuguese Jews, persecuted by the inquisition, stript of their fortunes, and banished to Brazil, introduced, by their example, some sort of order and industry among the transported felons and strumpets by whom that colony was originally peopled, and taught them the culture of the sugar-cane. Upon all these different occasions, it was not the wisdom and policy, but the disorder and injustice of the European governments, which peopled and cultivated America.
p84.zh: 英国的清教徒,在家中受约束,为自由而逃到美国,并在那里建立了新英格兰的四国政府.英国的天主教徒受到更不公正的待遇,他们建立了马里兰州;石匠,宾夕法尼亚州。 葡萄牙犹太人受到宗教裁判所的迫害,他们的财产被剥去,并被流放到巴西,他们以他们为例,在被运送的重罪犯和被贩卖的奴隶中引入某种秩序和产业,并教他们甘蔗文化。 在所有这些不同的场合,不是智慧和政策,而是欧洲政府的混乱和不公正,它们使美国人民得以生存和耕种。

p85.original: In effectuation some of the most important of these establishments, the different governments of Europe had as little merit as in projecting them. The conquest of Mexico was the project, not of the council of Spain, but of a governor of Cuba; and it was effectuated by the spirit of the bold adventurer to whom it was entrusted, in spite of every thing which that governor, who soon repented of having trusted such a person, could do to thwart it. The conquerors of Chili and Peru, and of almost all the other Spanish settlements upon the continent of America, carried out with them no other public encouragement, but a general permission to make settlements and conquests in the name of the king of Spain. Those adventures were all at the private risk and expense of the adventurers. The government of Spain contributed scarce any thing to any of them. That of England contributed as little towards effectuating the establishment of some of its most important colonies in North America.
p85.zh: 实际上,其中一些最重要的机构,欧洲各国政府在进行规划方面没有什么好处。 对墨西哥的征服不是西班牙议会的计划,而是古巴总督的计划;这是受委托给他的大胆冒险家的精神所促成的,尽管这位总督很快悔改了信任这样一个人,却可以做任何事情来挫败它。奇利和秘鲁的征服者,以及美洲大陆上几乎所有其他西班牙定居点的征服者,没有与他们一起进行任何其他的公开鼓励,而是普遍允许以西班牙国王的名义建立定居点和征服. 这些冒险都是冒险家们的私人冒险和牺牲品. 西班牙政府对此贡献甚少。英格兰对在北美建立一些最重要的殖民地的贡献很小。

p86.original: When those establishments were effectuated, and had become so considerable as to attract the attention of the mother country, the first regulations which she made with regard to them, had always in view to secure to herself the monopoly of their commerce; to confine their market, and to enlarge her own at their expense, and, consequently, rather to damp and discourage, than to quicken and forward the course of their prosperity. In the different ways in which this monopoly has been exercised, consists one of the most essential differences in the policy of the different European nations with regard to their colonies. The best of them all, that of England, is only somewhat less illiberal and oppressive than that of any of the rest.
p86.zh: 当这些企业生效并变得如此庞大,以致引起母国注意时,她对它们的最初规定总是是为了确保自己的商业垄断;限制它们的市场,并以它们为代价扩大自己的市场,因此是潮湿和气馁,而不是加速和推进它们的繁荣。以不同的方式行使这种垄断权,是不同欧洲国家对其殖民地政策中最根本的区别之一。 其中最好的,即英国的,只是比其他任何一个更不自由,更不具有压迫性.

p87.original: In what way, therefore, has the policy of Europe contributed either to the first establishment, or to the present grandeur of the colonies of America? In one way, and in one way only, it has contributed a good deal. Magna virum mater! It bred and formed the men who were capable of achieving such great actions, and of laying the foundation of so great an empire; and there is no other quarter of the world; of which the policy is capable of forming, or has ever actually, and in fact, formed such men. The colonies owe to the policy of Europe the education and great views of their active and enterprizing founders; and some of the greatest and most important of them, so far as concerns their internal government, owe to it scarce anything else.
p87.zh: 因此,欧洲的政策对第一个建立,或对美国殖民地目前的伟大者,有何种贡献?一种方式,也一种方式,它贡献了很好的交易. 大维鲁姆母校! 它培养并形成了那些有能力实现如此伟大行动,为如此伟大帝国奠定基础的人;世界上没有别的方面;其中政策能够形成,或曾经实际形成,事实上也形成了这样的人.殖民地应归功于欧洲的政策,是他们积极而生动的创始人的教育和伟大的观点;而其中一些最伟大和最重要的,就他们的内部政府而言,是因为它缺少其他东西。

p88.original: PART III. Of the Advantages which Europe has derived From the Discovery of America, and from that of a Passage to the East Indies by the Cape of Good Hope.
p88.zh: 第三编 欧洲从美国发现中衍生出来的优势 以及从好望角到东印度群岛的优势

p89.original: Such are the advantages which the colonies of America have derived from the policy of Europe.
p89.zh: 这就是美国殖民地从欧洲政策中获得的优势.

p90.original: What are those which Europe has derived from the discovery and colonization of America?
p90.zh: 欧洲从美国的发现和殖民化中得到了什么?

p91.original: Those advantages may be divided, first, into the general advantages which Europe, considered as one great country, has derived from those great events; and, secondly, into the particular advantages which each colonizing country has derived from the colonies which particularly belong to it, in consequence of the authority or dominion which it exercises over them.
p91.zh: 首先,这些好处可以分为欧洲作为一个伟大国家从这些重大事件中获得的一般好处;其次,每个殖民国家由于对其行使权力或统治权而从特别属于它的殖民地获得的特殊好处。

p92.original: The general advantages which Europe, considered as one great country, has derived from the discovery and colonization of America, consist, first, in the increase of its enjoyments; and, secondly, in the augmentation of its industry.
p92.zh: 欧洲作为一个伟大国家,从美国的发现和殖民化中获得了普遍的好处,首先是增加其享受;其次是增加其工业。

p93.original: The surplus produce of America imported into Europe, furnishes the inhabitants of this great continent with a variety of commodities which they could not otherwise have possessed; some for conveniency and use, some for pleasure, and some for ornament; and thereby contributes to increase their enjoyments.
p93.zh: 进口到欧洲的美国剩余农产品为这个大大陆的居民提供了他们本来不可能拥有的各种商品;有些是供娱乐和使用,有些是供娱乐,有些是供装饰品使用;因此有助于增加他们的享受。

p94.original: The discovery and colonization of America, it will readily be allowed, have contributed to augment the industry, first, of all the countries which trade to it directly, such as Spain, Portugal, France, and England; and, secondly, of all those which, without trading to it directly, send, through the medium of other countries, goods to it of their own produce, such as Austrian Flanders, and some provinces of Germany, which, through the medium of the countries before mentioned, send to it a considerable quantity of linen and other goods. All such countries have evidently gained a more extensive market for their surplus produce, and must consequently have been encouraged to increase its quantity.
p94.zh: 美国的发现和殖民化是很容易允许的,它有助于扩大工业,首先是直接向其贸易的所有国家,如西班牙、葡萄牙、法国和英格兰;其次是不直接向它贸易的所有国家,通过其他国家的媒介,向它运送本国产品的货物,如奥地利的佛兰德斯和德国的一些省份,它们通过上述国家的媒介,向它发送了大量的亚麻和其他货物。 所有这些国家显然都为其剩余产品赢得了更广泛的市场,因此必须鼓励它们增加其数量。

p95.original: But that those great events should likewise have contributed to encourage the industry of countries such as Hungary and Poland, which may never, perhaps, have sent a single commodity of their own produce to America, is not, perhaps, altogether so evident. That those events have done so, however, cannot be doubted. Some part of the produce of America is consumed in Hungary and Poland, and there is some demand there for the sugar, chocolate, and tobacco, of that new quarter of the world. But those commodities must be purchased with something which is either the produce of the industry of Hungary and Poland, or with something which had been purchased with some part of that produce. Those commodities of America are new values, new equivalents, introduced into Hungary and Poland, to be exchanged there for the surplus produce of these countries. By being carried thither, they create a new and more extensive market for that surplus produce. They raise its value, and thereby contribute to encourage its increase. Though no part of it may ever be carried to America, it may be carried to other countries, which purchase it with a part of their share of the surplus produce of America, and it may find a market by means of the circulation of that trade which was originally put into motion by the surplus produce of America.
p95.zh: 但是,这些重大事件同样应该有助于鼓励匈牙利和波兰等国的工业,也许这些国家从未将本国产品中的单一商品寄给美国,也许并不是完全如此明显。 然而,这些事件已经发生,这一点不容怀疑。 美国的部分产品在匈牙利和波兰消费,对世界新季度的糖、巧克力和烟草也有一些需求。 但是,这些商品必须用匈牙利和波兰工业的产品购买,或者用用其中一部分的产品购买。 美国的这些商品是匈牙利和波兰引进的新价值、新等价物,将在那里换取这些国家的剩余产品。 它们通过搬运,为这种剩余产品创造了一个新的和更加广泛的市场。 它们提高了其价值,从而有助于鼓励其增加。 尽管它的任何部分都不得运往美国,但可运往其他国家,这些国家用自己在美国剩余产品中所占的份额购买它,而且它可通过该贸易的流通找到市场,而该贸易最初是由美国剩余产品启动的。

p96.original: Those great events may even have contributed to increase the enjoyments, and to augment the industry, of countries which not only never sent any commodities to America, but never received any from it. Even such countries may have received a greater abundance of other commodities from countries, of which the surplus produce had been augmented by means of the American trade. This greater abundance, as it must necessarily have increased their enjoyments, so it must likewise have augmented their industry. A greater number of new equivalents, of some kind or other, must have been presented to them to be exchanged for the surplus produce of that industry. A more extensive market must have been created for that surplus produce, so as to raise its value, and thereby encourage its increase. The mass of commodities annually thrown into the great circle of European commerce, and by its various revolutions annually distributed among all the different nations comprehended within it, must have been augmented by the whole surplus produce of America. A greater share of this greater mass, therefore, is likely to have fallen to each of those nations, to have increased their enjoyments, and augmented their industry.
p96.zh: 这些重大事件甚至可能有助于提高那些不仅从未向美国发送过任何商品,而且从未从美国获得过商品的国家的享受,并增加其工业。 即使这些国家也可能从一些国家得到更多的其他商品,其中的剩余产品是通过美国贸易而增加的。 这种更大的丰度,因为它必然增加了他们的享受,因此,它同样也必然增加了他们的工业。必须向它们提交更多的新的等价物,某种等价物,以换取该行业的剩余产品。必须为这种剩余产品建立一个更广泛的市场,以提高其价值,从而鼓励其增加。 每年大量商品投入欧洲商业的大圈子,以及每年在它所理解的所有不同国家之间进行的各种革命,必定会因美国的全部剩余产品而增加。 因此,这些国家中每一个国家都有可能占到更大份额,增加享受,扩大工业。

p97.original: The exclusive trade of the mother countries tends to diminish, or at least to keep down below what they would otherwise rise to, both the enjoyments and industry of all those nations in general, and of the American colonies in particular. It is a dead weight upon the action of one of the great springs which puts into motion a great part of the business of mankind. By rendering the colony produce dearer in all other countries, it lessens its consumption, and thereby cramps the industry of the colonies, and both the enjoyments and the industry of all other countries, which both enjoy less when they pay more for what they enjoy, and produce less when they get less for what they produce. By rendering the produce of all other countries dearer in the colonies, it cramps in the same manner the industry of all other colonies, and both the enjoyments and the industry of the colonies. It is a clog which, for the supposed benefit of some particular countries, embarrasses the pleasures and encumbers the industry of all other countries, but of the colonies more than of any other. It not only excludes as much as possible all other countries from one particular market, but it confines as much as possible the colonies to one particular market; and the difference is very great between being excluded from one particular market when all others are open, and being confined to one particular market when all others are shut up. The surplus produce of the colonies, however, is the original source of all that increase of enjoyments and industry which Europe derives from the discovery and colonization of America, and the exclusive trade of the mother countries tends to render this source much less abundant than it otherwise would be.
p97.zh: 母国的专营贸易往往减少,或至少低于它们本来可以达到的程度,所有这些国家,特别是美洲殖民地的享受和工业。 它对一个伟大的泉水的行动是一死不活的,它使人类事业的很大一部分投入了行动。 它通过使殖民地在所有其他国家生产更加珍贵,减少其消费,从而紧缩殖民地的工业,以及所有其他国家的享受和工业,它们既在为所享受的利益付出更多报酬时享受较少,又在为所生产的利益获得较少报酬时享受较少。 它使所有其他国家的产品在殖民地更加珍贵,以同样的方式使所有其他殖民地的产业以及殖民地的享受和产业萎缩。 它是一个障碍,为某些特定国家的利益着想,它使所有其他国家,但殖民地的工业比任何其他国家更难堪和陷入困境。 它不仅尽可能地将所有其他国家排除在某一市场之外,而且尽可能将殖民地限制在一个特定市场;在所有其他国家开放时被排斥在某一市场之外,在所有其他国家关闭时被限制在一个特定市场之间,差别很大。 然而,殖民地的剩余产物是欧洲因美洲的发现和殖民化而增加的享受和工业的原始来源,而母国独有的贸易往往使这一来源比其他来源要少得多。

p98.original: The particular advantages which each colonizing country derives from the colonies which particularly belong to it, are of two different kinds; first, those common advantages which every empire derives from the provinces subject to its dominion; and, secondly, those peculiar advantages which are supposed to result from provinces of so very peculiar a nature as the European colonies of America.
p98.zh: 每个殖民国家的特殊优势来自特别属于它的殖民地,它们有两种不同的优势;第一,每个帝国都来自受其统治的省份的共同利益;第二,那些本应来自欧洲殖民地等性质非常特殊省份的特殊优势。

p99.original: The common advantages which every empire derives from the provinces subject to its dominion consist, first, in the military force which they furnish for its defence; and, secondly, in the revenue which they furnish for the support of its civil government. The Roman colonies furnished occasionally both the one and the other. The Greek colonies sometimes furnished a military force, but seldom any revenue. They seldom acknowledged themselves subject to the dominion of the mother city. They were generally her allies in war, but very seldom her subjects in peace.
p99.zh: 每个帝国从受其管辖的省份获得的共同好处首先包括它们为其防卫提供的军事力量;其次包括它们为支持其民政政府而提供的收入。罗马殖民地偶尔会同时拥有一个和另一个。 希腊殖民地有时提供军事力量,但很少获得任何收入. 他们很少承认自己受母城的统治。 他们一般是她在战争中的盟友,但很少是她的臣民和平相处.

p100.original: The European colonies of America have never yet furnished any military force for the defence of the mother country. The military force has never yet been sufficient for their own defence; and in the different wars in which the mother countries have been engaged, the defence of their colonies has generally occasioned a very considerable distraction of the military force of those countries. In this respect, therefore, all the European colonies have, without exception, been a cause rather of weakness than of strength to their respective mother countries.
p100.zh: 美国的欧洲殖民地从未为保卫祖国提供任何军事力量.军事力量从来不足以保卫自己;在母国所参与的不同战争中,保卫其殖民地一般都使这些国家的军事力量分心相当大. 因此,在这方面,所有欧洲殖民地无一例外地都是各自祖国软弱而不是力量的原因。

p101.original: The colonies of Spain and Portugal only have contributed any revenue towards the defence of the mother country, or the support of her civil government. The taxes which have been levied upon those of other European nations, upon those of England in particular, have seldom been equal to the expense laid out upon them in time of peace, and never sufficient to defray that which they occasioned in time of war. Such colonies, therefore, have been a source of expense, and not of revenue, to their respective mother countries.
p101.zh: 西班牙和葡萄牙的殖民地只捐出任何收入来保卫祖国,或得到其文官政府的支持.对其他欧洲国家,特别是对英格兰国家征收的税款,很少相当于和平时期对它们的费用,而且永远不足以支付他们在战争时期所支付的费用。 因此,这些殖民地一直是各自祖国的收入来源,而不是收入来源。

p102.original: The advantages of such colonies to their respective mother countries, consist altogether in those peculiar advantages which are supposed to result from provinces of so very peculiar a nature as the European colonies of America; and the exclusive trade, it is acknowledged, is the sole source of all those peculiar advantages.
p102.zh: 这种殖民地对各自祖国的优势完全在于那些本应产生于诸如欧洲殖民地等非常特殊性质的省份的特殊优势;人们承认,独家贸易是所有这些特殊优势的唯一来源。

p103.original: In consequence of this exclusive trade, all that part of the surplus produce of the English colonies, for example, which consists in what are called enumerated commodities, can be sent to no other country but England. Other countries must afterwards buy it of her. It must be cheaper, therefore, in England than it can be in any other country, and must contribute more to increase the enjoyments of England than those of any other country. It must likewise contribute more to encourage her industry. For all those parts of her own surplus produce which England exchanges for those enumerated commodities, she must get a better price than any other countries can get for the like parts of theirs, when they exchange them for the same commodities. The manufactures of England, for example, will purchase a greater quantity of the sugar and tobacco of her own colonies than the like manufactures of other countries can purchase of that sugar and tobacco. So far, therefore, as the manufactures of England and those of other countries are both to be exchanged for the sugar and tobacco of the English colonies, this superiority of price gives an encouragement to the former beyond what the latter can, in these circumstances, enjoy. The exclusive trade of the colonies, therefore, as it diminishes, or at least keeps down below what they would otherwise rise to, both the enjoyments and the industry of the countries which do not possess it, so it gives an evident advantage to the countries which do possess it over those other countries.
p103.zh: 由于这种专营贸易,例如,英国殖民地的剩余产品,包括所谓的商品,除了英格兰之外,其他任何国家都无法收到。其他国家事后必须买下她。 因此,在英国,它必须比在任何其他国家更便宜,必须比任何其他国家更有助于增加英格兰的享受。 同样,它也必须为鼓励她的产业做出更多贡献。 对于她自己剩余产品中英格兰用来交换所列举商品的所有部分,当其他国家以同样的商品交换这些商品时,她必须获得比其他国家更好的价格。 例如,英格兰的制造厂将购买更多其本国殖民地的糖和烟草,而其他国家类似的制造厂则可以购买这种糖和烟草。 因此,到目前为止,由于英格兰和其他国家的制造品都要换取英国殖民地的糖和烟草,这种价格的优越性使前者受到鼓励,超出后者在这种情况下能够享受的. 因此,殖民地的专营贸易,随着减少,或至少低于它们本来可以达到的水平,既享受也不拥有殖民地的国家的工业,因此,它使拥有殖民地的国家明显地比那些其他国家更有利。

p104.original: This advantage, however, will, perhaps, be found to be rather what may be called a relative than an absolute advantage, and to give a superiority to the country which enjoys it, rather by depressing the industry and produce of other countries, than by raising those of that particular country above what they would naturally rise to in the case of a free trade.
p104.zh: 然而,这种优势也许将被视为一种相对的而不是绝对的优势,并赋予享有这种优势的国家以优越性,而不是通过压制其他国家的工业和生产,而不是通过使该特定国家的工业和生产高于在自由贸易的情况下它们自然会达到的水平。

p105.original: The tobacco of Maryland and Virginia, for example, by means of the monopoly which England enjoys of it, certainly comes cheaper to England than it can do to France to whom England commonly sells a considerable part of it. But had France and all other European countries been at all times allowed a free trade to Maryland and Virginia, the tobacco of those colonies might by this time have come cheaper than it actually does, not only to all those other countries, but likewise to England. The produce of tobacco, in consequence of a market so much more extensive than any which it has hitherto enjoyed, might, and probably would, by this time have been so much increased as to reduce the profits of a tobacco plantation to their natural level with those of a corn plantation, which it is supposed they are still somewhat above. The price of tobacco might, and probably would, by this time have fallen somewhat lower than it is at present. An equal quantity of the commodities, either of England or of those other countries, might have purchased in Maryland and Virginia a greater quantity of tobacco than it can do at present, and consequently have been sold there for so much a better price. So far as that weed, therefore, can, by its cheapness and abundance, increase the enjoyments, or augment the industry, either of England or of any other country, it would probably, in the case of a free trade, have produced both these effects in somewhat a greater degree than it can do at present. England, indeed, would not, in this case, have had any advantage over other countries. She might have bought the tobacco of her colonies somewhat cheaper, and consequently have sold some of her own commodities somewhat dearer, than she actually does; but she could neither have bought the one cheaper, nor sold the other dearer, than any other country might have done. She might, perhaps, have gained an absolute, but she would certainly have lost a relative advantage.
p105.zh: 例如马里兰和弗吉尼亚的烟草,通过英格兰享有的垄断权,在英国的烟草当然比在法国便宜,因为英国通常向法国出售相当大一部分烟草。 但是如果法国和所有其他欧洲国家在任何时候都允许向马里兰州和弗吉尼亚州进行自由贸易,那么这些殖民地的烟草到现在可能已经比实际便宜,不仅对所有这些国家,而且对英格兰也是如此。烟草生产由于市场比以往任何市场都广泛得多,到现在可能已经增加很多,使烟草种植的利润与玉米种植的利润相提并论,因为玉米种植的利润可能仍然略高于此。烟草价格可能,而且可能届时已经比现在低一些。英国或其他国家等量的商品可能比目前购买的烟草数量多,因此以更好的价格出售给马里兰和弗吉尼亚。 因此,如果大麻的廉价和丰度能够增加英格兰或任何其他国家的享受或扩大工业,那么,在自由贸易的情况下,它可能比目前产生更大的程度的这两种影响。 在这种情况下,英格兰确实不会比其他国家有任何优势。 她可能买下了自己殖民地的烟草,因此卖出了她自己的一些商品,比她实际卖的要便宜一些;但她既买不到一个更便宜的商品,也卖掉另一个更亲爱的商品,比任何其他国家都便宜。 她也许已经获得了绝对的优势,但她肯定会失去相对优势.

p106.original: In order, however, to obtain this relative advantage in the colony trade, in order to execute the invidious and malignant project of excluding, as much as possible, other nations from any share in it, England, there are very probable reasons for believing, has not only sacrificed a part of the absolute advantage which she, as well as every other nation, might have derived from that trade, but has subjected herself both to an absolute and to a relative disadvantage in almost every other branch of trade.
p106.zh: 然而,为了在殖民地贸易中取得这种相对优势,为了执行尽可能将其他国家排除在其中任何份额的令人发指的恶毒计划,英国有非常可能的理由相信,它不仅牺牲了她和任何其他国家可能从这种贸易中获得的部分绝对优势,而且使自己在几乎所有其他贸易分支中都处于绝对和相对劣势的地位。

p107.original: When, by the act of navigation, England assumed to herself the monopoly of the colony trade, the foreign capitals which had before been employed in it, were necessarily withdrawn from it. The English capital, which had before carried on but a part of it, was now to carry on the whole. The capital which had before supplied the colonies with but a part of the goods which they wanted from Europe, was now all that was employed to supply them with the whole. But it could not supply them with the whole; and the goods with which it did supply them were necessarily sold very dear. The capital which had before bought but a part of the surplus produce of the colonies, was now all that was employed to buy the whole. But it could not buy the whole at any thing near the old price; and therefore, whatever it did buy, it necessarily bought very cheap. But in an employment of capital, in which the merchant sold very dear, and bought very cheap, the profit must have been very great, and much above the ordinary level of profit in other branches of trade. This superiority of profit in the colony trade could not fail to draw from other branches of trade a part of the capital which had before been employed in them. But this revulsion of capital, as it must have gradually increased the competition of capitals in the colony trade, so it must have gradually diminished that competition in all those other branches of trade; as it must have gradually lowered the profits of the one, so it must have gradually raised those of the other, till the profits of all came to a new level, different from, and somewhat higher, than that at which they had been before.
p107.zh: 当英格兰通过航海行为,自己承担了殖民地贸易的垄断权时,以前受雇于该地的外国首都就必然被退出。英国的首都,以前只延续了一部分,现在要继续整体发展。 以前只向殖民地供应了一部分他们想要从欧洲得到的货物的首都,现在已是用来供应全部货物的。 但是,它不能提供全部货物;它确实提供的货物必然是十分珍贵的。 以前购买了一部分殖民地剩余产物的资本,现在全部用于购买整个殖民地。 但是,它不能买到所有接近旧价格的东西;因此,无论它买什么,它必然买的非常便宜。 但是,在一种资本的雇佣中,商人卖得非常珍贵,买得非常便宜,利润一定非常大,大大高于其他贸易分支的普通利润水平.殖民地贸易中利润的这种优越性不能不从以前受雇于其他贸易分支的资本中提取。 但这种资本的反弹,因为它必然逐渐增加了殖民地贸易中各国首都的竞争,所以它必然逐渐减少了所有其他贸易分支的竞争;因为它必然逐渐降低了一方的利润,所以它必然逐渐提高了另一方的利润,直到所有人利润都达到了一个新的水平,与以前不同,而且有些高。

p108.original: This double effect of drawing capital from all other trades, and of raising the rate of profit somewhat higher than it otherwise would have been in all trades, was not only produced by this monopoly upon its first establishment, but has continued to be produced by it ever since.
p108.zh: 这种从所有其他贸易中提取资本以及提高利润率的双重效应,比其他所有贸易中都高一些,不仅是这种垄断对其第一个机构造成的,而且从那时起一直由它产生。

p109.original: First, This monopoly has been continually drawing capital from all other trades, to be employed in that of the colonies.
p109.zh: 第一,这种垄断不断从所有其他贸易中吸引资本,用于殖民地。

p110.original: Though the wealth of Great Britain has increased very much since the establishment of the act of navigation, it certainly has not increased in the same proportion as that or the colonies. But the foreign trade of every country naturally increases in proportion to its wealth, its surplus produce in proportion to its whole produce; and Great Britain having engrossed to herself almost the whole of what may be called the foreign trade of the colonies, and her capital not having increased in the same proportion as the extent of that trade, she could not carry it on without continually withdrawing from other branches of trade some part of the capital which had before been employed in them, as well as withholding from them a great deal more which would otherwise have gone to them. Since the establishment of the act of navigation, accordingly, the colony trade has been continually increasing, while many other branches of foreign trade, particularly of that to other parts of Europe, have been continually decaying. Our manufactures for foreign sale, instead of being suited, as before the act of navigation, to the neighbouring market of Europe, or to the more distant one of the countries which lie round the Mediterranean sea, have the greater part of them, been accommodated to the still more distant one of the colonies; to the market in which they have the monopoly, rather than to that in which they have many competitors. The causes of decay in other branches of foreign trade, which, by Sir Matthew Decker and other writers, have been sought for in the excess and improper mode of taxation, in the high price of labour, in the increase of luxury, etc. may all be found in the overgrowth of the colony trade. The mercantile capital of Great Britain, though very great, yet not being infinite, and though greatly increased since the act of navigation, yet not being increased in the same proportion as the colony trade, that trade could not possibly be carried on without withdrawing some part of that capital from other branches of trade, nor consequently without some decay of those other branches.
p110.zh: 虽然大不列颠的财富自航海行为建立以来已经大大增加,但显然并没有以与这个或殖民地相同的比例增加. 但是,每个国家的对外贸易自然会根据其财富的比例增加,其剩余产值占其全部产值的比例增加;大不列颠几乎把可以称为殖民地对外贸易的全部内容都塞入了自己手中,而其资本的增长比例与这种贸易的程度不相上下,她不能继续从以前受雇于它们的部分资本的其他贸易分支中撤出,并且从它们那里扣下大量本来会流向它们的资本。 因此,自航海行为确立以来,殖民地贸易一直在增加,而许多其他外贸部门,特别是向欧洲其他地区的贸易部门,则在不断衰败。 我们用于外国销售的制成品,不是像航海行为之前那样适合向邻近的欧洲市场或较遥远的环地中海国家出售的,而是更多地供那些仍然比较遥远的殖民地使用;供它们垄断的市场使用,而不是供它们拥有许多竞争对手的市场使用。 马修·德克尔爵士和其他作家认为,在过度和不当的征税方式、高劳动力价格、奢侈品增加等情况下寻求外贸其他部门衰败的原因,都可能出现在殖民地贸易的过度增长中。 大不列颠的商贸资本虽然非常巨大,但并非无限,虽然自航海行为以来大幅增加,但与殖民地贸易的比例没有相同增加,但如果不从其他贸易分支撤出部分资本,或者不因此使其他贸易分支出现某种衰落,贸易就不可能继续进行。

p111.original: England, it must be observed, was a great trading country, her mercantile capital was very great, and likely to become still greater and greater every day, not only before the act of navigation had established the monopoly of the corn trade, but before that trade was very considerable. In the Dutch war, during the government of Cromwell, her navy was superior to that of Holland; and in that which broke out in the beginning of the reign of Charles II., it was at least equal, perhaps superior to the united navies of France and Holland. Its superiority, perhaps, would scarce appear greater in the present times, at least if the Dutch navy were to bear the same proportion to the Dutch commerce now which it did then. But this great naval power could not, in either of those wars, be owing to the act of navigation. During the first of them, the plan of that act had been but just formed; and though, before the breaking out of the second, it had been fully enacted by legal authority, yet no part of it could have had time to produce any considerable effect, and least of all that part which established the exclusive trade to the colonies. Both the colonies and their trade were inconsiderable then, in comparison of what they are how. The island of Jamaica was an unwholesome desert, little inhabited, and less cultivated. New York and New Jersey were in the possession of the Dutch, the half of St. Christopher's in that of the French. The island of Antigua, the two Carolinas, Pennsylvania, Georgia, and Nova Scotia, were not planted. Virginia, Maryland, and New England were planted; and though they were very thriving colonies, yet there was not perhaps at that time, either in Europe or America, a single person who foresaw, or even suspected, the rapid progress which they have since made in wealth, population, and improvement. The island of Barbadoes, in short, was the only British colony of any consequence, of which the condition at that time bore any resemblance to what it is at present. The trade of the colonies, of which England, even for some time after the act of navigation, enjoyed but a part (for the act of navigation was not very strictly executed till several years after it was enacted), could not at that time be the cause of the great trade of England, nor of the great naval power which was supported by that trade. The trade which at that time supported that great naval power was the trade of Europe, and of the countries which lie round the Mediterranean sea. But the share which Great Britain at present enjoys of that trade could not support any such great naval power. Had the growing trade of the colonies been left free to all nations, whatever share of it might have fallen to Great Britain, and a very considerable share would probably have fallen to her, must have been all an addition to this great trade of which she was before in possession. In consequence of the monopoly, the increase of the colony trade has not so much occasioned an addition to the trade which Great Britain had before, as a total change in its direction.
p111.zh: 必须指出,英格兰是一个伟大的贸易国,她的商贸资本非常巨大,而且可能每天变大,不仅在航海行为确立玉米贸易的垄断之前,而且在这种贸易变得非常可观之前. 在荷兰战争中,克伦威尔政府时期,她的海军优于荷兰;在查理二世统治初期爆发的战役中,它至少是平等的,也许优于法国和荷兰的统一海军.其优越性,也许在当今时代似乎并不大,至少如果荷兰海军现在承担荷兰商业的同样比例的话。 但是,在其中任何一个战争中,这个伟大的海军力量都不可能是航行行为造成的。 在其中第一个阶段,这一法案的计划刚刚形成;虽然在第二个阶段爆发之前,它已经完全由法律当局颁布,但其中任何部分都不可能产生任何相当的效果,尤其是那些建立对殖民地的专属贸易的部分。 当时,殖民地及其贸易都微不足道,与其如何比较。 牙买加岛是一片荒漠,人烟稀少,耕地较少。纽约和新泽西州由荷兰人占有,是圣塔的半个地区.克里斯托弗是法国人 安提瓜岛,两个卡罗来纳州,宾夕法尼亚州,乔治亚州,和新斯科舍州都没有栽培.弗吉尼亚、马里兰和新英格兰被种植;虽然它们是非常繁荣的殖民地,但也许当时在欧洲或美国都没有一个人预见,甚至怀疑他们从那时起在财富、人口和改善方面取得的迅速进展。简而言之,巴巴多斯岛是英国唯一一个造成任何后果的殖民地,当时的状况与现在的情况完全相似。殖民地的贸易,英格兰即使在航海行为之后的一段时间内也享有但一部分(因为航海行为在颁布几年后才被严格实施),在当时不可能是英格兰大贸易的起因,也不能是这种贸易所支持的海军大国的起因. 当时支持这一伟大海军力量的贸易是欧洲的贸易,以及环地中海国家的贸易。 但是,英国目前享有的这种贸易份额不能支持任何如此强大的海军力量。 如果殖民地不断增长的贸易被留给所有国家自由,无论它中的任何一部分可能落在大不列颠身上,而且很可能有相当大一部分落在她身上,那必定是她以前拥有的这一巨大贸易之外的一个补充。 由于垄断,殖民地贸易的增加并没有像大不列颠以前那样增加贸易,使其方向完全改变。

p112.original: Secondly, This monopoly has necessarily contributed to keep up the rate of profit, in all the different branches of British trade, higher than it naturally would have been, had all nations been allowed a free trade to the British colonies.
p112.zh: 第二,如果允许所有国家向英国殖民地进行自由贸易,这种垄断必然有助于保持利润率,在英国贸易的所有不同分支中,利润率都高于自然会高。

p113.original: The monopoly of the colony trade, as it necessarily drew towards that trade a greater proportion of the capital of Great Britain than what would have gone to it of its own accord, so, by the expulsion of all foreign capitals, it necessarily reduced the whole quantity of capital employed in that trade below what it naturally would have been in the case of a free trade. But, by lessening the competition of capitals in that branch of trade, it necessarily raised the rate of profit in that branch. By lessening, too, the competition of British capitals in all other branches of trade, it necessarily raised the rate of British profit in all those other branches. Whatever may have been, at any particular period since the establishment of the act of navigation, the state or extent of the mercantile capital of Great Britain, the monopoly of the colony trade must, during the continuance of that state, have raised the ordinary rate of British profit higher than it otherwise would have been, both in that and in all the other branches of British trade. If, since the establishment of the act of navigation, the ordinary rate of British profit has fallen considerably, as it certainly has, it must have fallen still lower, had not the monopoly established by that act contributed to keep it up.
p113.zh: 殖民地贸易的垄断性,因为它必然使大不列颠的资本比它本该拥有的资本多得多,因此,通过驱逐所有外国资本,它必然使该贸易中所使用的资本总量低于自由贸易中它自然会拥有的资本。 但是,通过减少该贸易分支中各国首都的竞争,它必然提高了该分支的利润率。 通过减少所有其他贸易分支中英国首都的竞争,它必然提高英国在所有其他分支的利润率。不论在航海行为确立以来的任何特定时期,在大不列颠的商贸资本的状态或范围,殖民地贸易的垄断,在英国继续经营期间,必须提高英国正常利润率,无论在英国贸易的这一环节还是在所有其他分支,都比本来会提高。 如果自航行行为确立以来,英国的正常利润率已经大幅度下降,当然,它一定已经下降,但这一行为所建立的垄断并没有有助于保持下去。

p114.original: But whatever raises, in any country, the ordinary rate of profit higher than it otherwise would be, necessarily subjects that country both to an absolute, and to a relative disadvantage in every branch of trade of which she has not the monopoly.
p114.zh: 但是,在任何国家,无论提高利润的正常比率高于其他水平,都必然使该国处于绝对地位,并在她没有垄断的每一个贸易部门处于相对不利的地位。

p115.original: It subjects her to an absolute disadvantage; because, in such branches of trade, her merchants cannot get this greater profit without selling dearer than they otherwise would do, both the goods of foreign countries which they import into their own, and the goods of their own country which they export to foreign countries. Their own country must both buy dearer and sell dearer; must both buy less, and sell less; must both enjoy less and produce less, than she otherwise would do.
p115.zh: 它使她处于绝对不利的地位;因为在这种贸易分支中,她的商人如果不出售他们自己进口的外国货物和他们出口到外国的本国货物,就得不到如此巨大的利润。 他们自己的国家必须既购买亲爱的人,又出售亲爱的人;必须既少购买,又少出售;必须既少享受,又少生产,否则她就会这样做。

p116.original: It subjects her to a relative disadvantage; because, in such branches of trade, it sets other countries, which are not subject to the same absolute disadvantage, either more above her or less below her, than they otherwise would be. It enables them both to enjoy more and to produce more, in proportion to what she enjoys and produces. It renders their superiority greater, or their inferiority less, than it otherwise would be. By raising the price of her produce above what it otherwise would be, it enables the merchants of other countries to undersell her in foreign markets, and thereby to justle her out of almost all those branches of trade, of which she has not the monopoly.
p116.zh: 它使她处于相对不利的地位;因为在这种贸易部门,它使其他国家处于同样的绝对不利地位,它们要么高于她,要么低于她,否则它们就会低于她。这使得她们既能享受更多,又能生产更多,与她们所享受和生产的程度成比例。 它使得他们的优越性或自卑性比其他情况更大或更低。 通过提高她的农产品价格,使其价格高于本来会的价格,使其他国家的商人得以在外国市场向她出售,从而将她从几乎所有的贸易分支中解放出来,而她并不垄断这些贸易分支。

p117.original: Our merchants frequently complain of the high wages of British labour, as the cause of their manufactures being undersold in foreign markets; but they are silent about the high profits of stock. They complain of the extravagant gain of other people; but they say nothing of their own. The high profits of British stock, however, may contribute towards raising the price of British manufactures, in many cases, as much, and in some perhaps more, than the high wages of British labour.
p117.zh: 我们的商人经常抱怨英国劳工的高工资,因为他们的制成品在外国市场被低价出售;但他们对股票的高利润却保持沉默。 他们怨恨别人的奢侈,但他们自言自语。 然而,英国股票的高利润可能有助于提高英国制造品的价格,在许多情况下,可能比英国劳动力的高工资高得多。

p118.original: It is in this manner that the capital of Great Britain, one may justly say, has partly been drawn and partly been driven from the greater part of the different branches of trade of which she has not the monopoly; from the trade of Europe, in particular, and from that of the countries which lie round the Mediterranean sea.
p118.zh: 可以说,大不列颠的首都正是以这种方式从她没有垄断的很大一部分贸易分支中抽取和部分地从欧洲贸易,特别是从地中海沿岸国家贸易中抽取。

p119.original: It has partly been drawn from those branches of trade, by the attraction of superior profit in the colony trade, in consequence of the continual increase of that trade, and of the continual insufficiency of the capital which had carried it on one year to carry it on the next.
p119.zh: 这部分地来自这些贸易分支,由于殖民地贸易不断增长而吸引了优势利润,以及由于在下一年中承载该贸易的资本持续不足而吸引了这些贸易分支。

p120.original: It has partly been driven from them, by the advantage which the high rate of profit established in Great Britain gives to other countries, in all the different branches of trade of which Great Britain has not the monopoly.
p120.zh: 它部分地被它们所驱使,因为大不列颠建立的高利润率给其他国家带来优势,在大不列颠没有垄断的所有不同的贸易分支中.

p121.original: As the monopoly of the colony trade has drawn from those other branches a part of the British capital, which would otherwise have been employed in them, so it has forced into them many foreign capitals which would never have gone to them, had they not been expelled from the colony trade. In those other branches of trade, it has diminished the competition of British capitals, and thereby raised the rate of British profit higher than it otherwise would have been. On the contrary, it has increased the competition of foreign capitals, and thereby sunk the rate of foreign profit lower than it otherwise would have been. Both in the one way and in the other, it must evidently have subjected Great Britain to a relative disadvantage in all those other branches of trade.
p121.zh: 由于殖民地贸易的垄断来自这些其他分支,因此,英国资本的一部分本来会受雇于这些分支,因此,它迫使这些分支拥有许多外国资本,如果不将他们逐出殖民地贸易,这些外国资本就永远不会去。 在那些其他贸易分支中,它削弱了英国首都的竞争,从而提高了英国的利润率,比本来可以达到的要高. 相反,它增加了外国首都的竞争,从而使外国利润率低于本该达到的水平。无论是从某种角度还是从另一种角度来说,它显然都使大不列颠在所有其他贸易分支中处于相对不利的地位。

p122.original: The colony trade, however, it may perhaps be said, is more advantageous to Great Britain than any other; and the monopoly, by forcing into that trade a greater proportion of the capital of Great Britain than what would otherwise have gone to it, has turned that capital into an employment, more advantageous to the country than any other which it could have found.
p122.zh: 然而,也许可以说,殖民地贸易对大不列颠比任何其他国家都更有利;垄断通过将大不列颠资本的更大比例强制投入到这种贸易中,使这种资本变成了一种就业,比它可能找到的任何其他国家都更有利。

p123.original: The most advantageous employment of any capital to the country to which it belongs, is that which maintains there the greatest quantity of productive labour, and increases the most the annual produce of the land and labour of that country. But the quantity of productive labour which any capital employed in the foreign trade of consumption can maintain, is exactly in proportion, it has been shown in the second book, to the frequency of its returns. A capital of a thousand pounds, for example, employed in a foreign trade of consumption, of which the returns are made regularly once in the year, can keep in constant employment, in the country to which it belongs, a quantity of productive labour, equal to what a thousand pounds can maintain there for a year. If the returns are made twice or thrice in the year, it can keep in constant employment a quantity of productive labour, equal to what two or three thousand pounds can maintain there for a year. A foreign trade of consumption carried on with a neighbouring, is, upon that account, in general, more advantageous than one carried on with a distant country; and, for the same reason, a direct foreign trade of consumption, as it has likewise been shown in the second book, is in general more advantageous than a round-about one.
p123.zh: 任何资本对其所属国家最有利的就业,就是维持最多数量的生产性劳动力,并增加该国土地和劳动力的年产量。 但是,消费外贸中任何资本能够维持的生产性劳动力的数量,与第二本书所示的其回报频率完全成正比。 例如,在对外消费贸易中就业的一千英镑资本,每年定期获得一次回报,就可以在它所属的国家内保持恒定就业,一定数量的生产劳动,相当于1000英镑在那里维持一年的时间. 如果一年两次或三次获得回报,它可以使一定数量的生产劳动力持续就业,相当于每年在那里维持2至3 000磅。与邻国进行的对外消费贸易,总的来说比与遥远国家进行的对外消费贸易更有利;出于同样的原因,正如第二本书中同样表明的那样,直接对外消费贸易一般比环形贸易更有利。

p124.original: But the monopoly of the colony trade, so far as it has operated upon the employment of the capital of Great Britain, has, in all cases, forced some part of it from a foreign trade of consumption carried on with a neighbouring, to one carried on with a more distant country, and in many cases from a direct foreign trade of consumption to a round-about one.
p124.zh: 但是,殖民地贸易的垄断,只要是在大不列颠首都就业的情况下进行的,就已迫使一部分殖民地贸易从与邻国进行的对外消费贸易,到与一个较远的国家进行的对外消费贸易,在许多情况下从直接对外消费贸易到环绕外国消费贸易。

p125.original: First, The monopoly of the colony trade has, in all cases, forced some part of the capital of Great Britain from a foreign trade of consumption carried on with a neighbouring, to one carried on with a more distant country.
p125.zh: 第一,殖民地贸易的垄断,在所有情况下,都迫使大不列颠首都的部分地区从与邻国进行的对外消费贸易转向与一个较远国家进行的对外消费贸易。

p126.original: It has, in all cases, forced some part of that capital from the trade with Europe, and with the countries which lie round the Mediterranean sea, to that with the more distant regions of America and the West Indies; from which the returns are necessarily less frequent, not only on account of the greater distance, but on account of the peculiar circumstances of those countries. New colonies, it has already been observed, are always understocked. Their capital is always much less than what they could employ with great profit and advantage in the improvement and cultivation of their land. They have a constant demand, therefore, for more capital than they have of their own; and, in order to supply the deficiency of their own, they endeavour to borrow as much as they can of the mother country, to whom they are, therefore, always in debt. The most common way in which the colonies contract this debt, is not by borrowing upon bond of the rich people of the mother country, though they sometimes do this too, but by running as much in arrear to their correspondents, who supply them with goods from Europe, as those correspondents will allow them. Their annual returns frequently do not amount to more than a third, and sometimes not to so great a proportion of what they owe. The whole capital, therefore, which their correspondents advance to them, is seldom returned to Britain in less than three, and sometimes not in less than four or five years. But a British capital of a thousand pounds, for example, which is returned to Great Britain only once in five years, can keep in constant employment only one-fifth part of the British industry which it could maintain, if the whole was returned once in the year; and, instead of the quantity of industry which a thousand pounds could maintain for a year, can keep in constant employment the quantity only which two hundred pounds can maintain for a year. The planter, no doubt, by the high price which he pays for the goods from Europe, by the interest upon the bills which he grants at distant dates, and by the commission upon the renewal of those which he grants at near dates, makes up, and probably more than makes up, all the loss which his correspondent can sustain by this delay. But, though he make up the loss of his correspondent, he cannot make up that of Great Britain. In a trade of which the returns are very distant, the profit of the merchant may be as great or greater than in one in which they are very frequent and near; but the advantage of the country in which he resides, the quantity of productive labour constantly maintained there, the annual produce of the land and labour, must always be much less. That the returns of the trade to America, and still more those of that to the West Indies, are, in general, not only more distant, but more irregular and more uncertain, too, than those of the trade to any part of Europe, or even of the countries which lie round the Mediterranean sea, will readily be allowed, I imagine, by everybody who has any experience of those different branches of trade.
p126.zh: 在所有情况下,它迫使该资本的一部分从与欧洲和与地中海沿岸国家的贸易中转移到与美洲和西印度群岛较远地区的贸易中;从这些贸易中返回的频率必然较低,不仅因为距离较远,而且因为这些国家的特殊情况。已经观察到,新殖民地总是储存不足。 他们的资本总是远远低于他们在改良和耕种土地方面能够以巨大的利润和优势来利用的资金。 因此,他们不断要求获得比自己拥有的更多的资本;为了供应自己的不足,他们尽量向母国借款,因此,他们总是欠债。殖民地签订这种债务的最常见方式不是借借祖国富人的债券,虽然他们有时也这样做,而是像那些通讯员所允许的那样,向他们的通讯员提供来自欧洲的货物。 他们每年的回报往往不超过三分之一,有时也不到他们所欠债务的很大比例。 因此,他们的通讯员推进到他们的整个首都,很少在不到3年的时间里返回英国,有时在不到4年或5年的时间里返回英国。 但是,比如说,英国的一千磅资本,五年内只归还一次,只要全年归还一次,它就能够维持的英国工业的五分之一就能够持续就业;而且,不象一千磅能够维持一年的工业数量那样,能够维持一年只有二百磅能够维持的工业数量。 毫无疑问,种植园主从欧洲支付高价货款,远期给付的账单利息,以及他在近日给付的账单续期时的佣金,弥补了,而且可能不止是弥补他的通讯员因这一拖延而能够承受的所有损失。 但是,虽然他弥补了通讯员的损失,但他无法弥补大不列颠的损失. 在回报非常遥远的行业中,商人的利润可能比他们经常和接近的行业要大或更大;但是,他居住的国家的优势,在那里不断维持的生产性劳动力的数量,土地和劳动力的年产量,必须总是少得多. 我认为,对美国贸易的回报,以及对西印度群岛贸易的回报,总的来说不仅比对欧洲任何地区贸易的回报更为遥远,而且比对地中海沿岸国家贸易的回报更不规则和更加不确定,这很容易被拥有这些不同贸易分支经验的每一个人所允许。

p127.original: Secondly, The monopoly of the colony trade, has, in many cases, forced some part of the capital of Great Britain from a direct foreign trade of consumption, into a round-about one.
p127.zh: 第二,殖民地贸易的垄断,在许多情况下,迫使大不列颠的首都的一部分从直接的对外消费贸易中转入环形贸易。

p128.original: Among the enumerated commodities which can be sent to no other market but Great Britain, there are several of which the quantity exceeds very much the consumption of Great Britain, and of which, a part, therefore, must be exported to other countries. But this cannot be done without forcing some part of the capital of Great Britain into a round-about foreign trade of consumption. Maryland, and Virginia, for example, send annually to Great Britain upwards of ninety-six thousand hogsheads of tobacco, and the consumption of Great Britain is said not to exceed fourteen thousand. Upwards of eighty-two thousand hogsheads, therefore, must be exported to other countries, to France, to Holland, and, to the countries which lie round the Baltic and Mediterranean seas. But that part of the capital of Great Britain which brings those eighty-two thousand hogsheads to Great Britain, which re-exports them from thence to those other countries, and which brings back from those other countries to Great Britain either goods or money in return, is employed in a round-about foreign trade of consumption; and is necessarily forced into this employment, in order to dispose of this great surplus. If we would compute in how many years the whole of this capital is likely to come back to Great Britain, we must add to the distance of the American returns that of the returns from those other countries. If, in the direct foreign trade of consumption which we carry on with America, the whole capital employed frequently does not come back in less than three or four years, the whole capital employed in this round-about one is not likely to come back in less than four or five. If the one can keep in constant employment but a third or a fourth part of the domestic industry which could be maintained by a capital returned once in the year, the other can keep in constant employment but a fourth or a fifth part of that industry. At some of the outports a credit is commonly given to those foreign correspondents to whom they export them tobacco. At the port of London, indeed, it is commonly sold for ready money: the rule is Weigh and pay. At the port of London, therefore, the final returns of the whole round-about trade are more distant than the returns from America, by the time only which the goods may lie unsold in the warehouse; where, however, they may sometimes lie long enough. But, had not the colonies been confined to the market of Great Britain for the sale of their tobacco, very little more of it would probably have come to us than what was necessary for the home consumption. The goods which Great Britain purchases at present for her own consumption with the great surplus of tobacco which she exports to other countries, she would, in this case, probably have purchased with the immediate produce of her own industry, or with some part of her own manufactures. That produce, those manufactures, instead of being almost entirely suited to one great market, as at present, would probably have been fitted to a great number of smaller markets. Instead of one great round-about foreign trade of consumption, Great Britain would probably have carried on a great number of small direct foreign trades of the same kind. On account of the frequency of the returns, a part, and probably but a small part, perhaps not above a third or a fourth of the capital which at present carries on this great round-about trade, might have been sufficient to carry on all those small direct ones; might have kept inconstant employment an equal quantity of British industry; and have equally supported the annual produce of the land and labour of Great Britain. All the purposes of this trade being, in this manner, answered by a much smaller capital, there would have been a large spare capital to apply to other purposes; to improve the lands, to increase the manufactures, and to extend the commerce of Great Britain; to come into competition at least with the other British capitals employed in all those different ways, to reduce the rate of profit in them all, and thereby to give to Great Britain, in all of them, a superiority over other countries, still greater than what she at present enjoys.
p128.zh: 在所列商品中,除了大不列颠以外,其他商品都无法运至其他市场,其中几种商品的数量远远超过大不列颠的消费,因此,其中一部分商品必须出口到其他国家。 但是,如果不迫使大不列颠的某部分首都进行环形的对外消费贸易,这一点是无法做到的. 例如,马里兰州和弗吉尼亚州每年向大不列颠发送96,000头猪头烟草,据说大不列颠的消费不超过14,000头。 因此,八万二千头猪必须出口到其他国家、法国、荷兰以及波罗的海和地中海周边国家。 但是,大不列颠的首都将这八万二千只猪头带到大不列颠,再从那里出口到那些其他国家,又从那些其他国家带回大不列颠的货物或金钱作为回报的那部分,却被雇佣在环绕的对外消费贸易中;为了处置这一巨大的盈余,必然被迫从事这种工作. 如果我们计算出这整个首都在几年内可能回到大不列颠,我们必须增加美国从这些国家返回的距离。 如果在与美国直接进行的对外消费贸易中,所雇用的全部资本在不到三、四年的时间里往往不会回来,那么在这个绕行的回合中雇用的全部资本在不到四、五年的时间里就不会回来。 如果一个人能够持续就业,但国内工业的第三或第四部分可由一年中一次返还的资本来维持,则另一部分可以持续就业,但该行业的第四或第五部分除外。在一些出口点,通常向向这些出口烟草的外国通讯员提供信贷。在伦敦港,的确,它通常为准备钱而出售:规则是维和支付. 因此,在伦敦港,整个环城贸易的最终回报比从美国的回报要远,到货物可能无法出售在仓库中的时候;然而,有时它们可能停留的时间足够长。 但是,如果没有殖民地被限制在大不列颠市场销售他们的烟草,那么,它们中可能来到我们的手中的远远没有像家庭消费所必需的那样多。英国目前购买的商品是她自己消费的,而她向其他国家出口的烟草大量过剩,在这种情况下,她很可能是用她自己的工业的即期产品或她自己的部分制成品购买的。 这些产品,而不是象目前这样几乎完全适合一个大市场,很可能已经配属于许多较小的市场。 大不列颠可能不会进行环绕一大圈的对外消费贸易,而是会进行大量同类的小型直接对外贸易。 由于返回的频繁性,一部分,也许只是一小部分,也许不超过目前从事这一大环路贸易的三分之一或四分之一的首都,可能足以维持所有这些小的直接贸易;可能使不稳定的就业保持英国工业的同等数量;并且同样支持大不列颠的土地和劳动力年产量。 这种贸易的所有目的,都以这种方式,由一个小得多的资本来回答,本来会有一大块剩余资本来应用到其他目的;改善土地,增加制成品,扩大大不列颠的商业;至少同以所有这些不同方式雇用的其他英国首都进行竞争,降低它们所有的利润率,从而让大不列颠在它们中都比其他国家优越,仍然比她现在所享受的还要多.

p129.original: The monopoly of the colony trade, too, has forced some part of the capital of Great Britain from all foreign trade of consumption to a carrying trade; and, consequently from supporting more or less the industry of Great Britain, to be employed altogether in supporting partly that of the colonies, and partly that of some other countries.
p129.zh: 殖民地贸易的垄断也迫使大不列颠的部分资本从所有消费的对外贸易转向承载贸易;因此,由于多少支持大不列颠的工业,完全被雇用来部分支持殖民地,部分支持其他一些国家。

p130.original: The goods, for example, which are annually purchased with the great surplus of eighty-two thousand hogsheads of tobacco annually re-exported from Great Britain, are not all consumed in Great Britain. Part of them, linen from Germany and Holland, for example, is returned to the colonies for their particular consumption. But that part of the capital of Great Britain which buys the tobacco with which this linen is afterwards bought, is necessarily withdrawn from supporting the industry of Great Britain, to be employed altogether in supporting, partly that of the colonies, and partly that of the particular countries who pay for this tobacco with the produce of their own industry.
p130.zh: 例如,每年从大不列颠再出口的八万二千只猪头烟草大量剩余地购买的商品,并不是全部在大不列颠消费。 其中一部分,例如来自德国和荷兰的亚麻,被送回殖民地,以供他们特定消费. 但是,大不列颠的首都购买烟叶的这一部分,在购买后,该烟叶的买主必须退出支持大不列颠的工业,完全用于支持,部分是殖民地的,部分是那些用本国工业的产物为这种烟草付费的国家。

p131.original: The monopoly of the colony trade, besides, by forcing towards it a much greater proportion of the capital of Great Britain than what would naturally have gone to it, seems to have broken altogether that natural balance which would otherwise have taken place among all the different branches of British industry. The industry of Great Britain, instead of being accommodated to a great number of small markets, has been principally suited to one great market. Her commerce, instead of running in a great number of small channels, has been taught to run principally in one great channel. But the whole system of her industry and commerce has thereby been rendered less secure; the whole state of her body politic less healthful than it otherwise would have been. In her present condition, Great Britain resembles one of those unwholesome bodies in which some of the vital parts are overgrown, and which, upon that account, are liable to many dangerous disorders, scarce incident to those in which all the parts are more properly proportioned. A small stop in that great blood-vessel, which has been artificially swelled beyond its natural dimensions, and through which an unnatural proportion of the industry and commerce of the country has been forced to circulate, is very likely to bring on the most dangerous disorders upon the whole body politic. The expectation of a rupture with the colonies, accordingly, has struck the people of Great Britain with more terror than they ever felt for a Spanish armada, or a French invasion. It was this terror, whether well or ill grounded, which rendered the repeal of the stamp act, among the merchants at least, a popular measure. In the total exclusion from the colony market, was it to last only for a few years, the greater part of our merchants used to fancy that they foresaw an entire stop to their trade; the greater part of our master manufacturers, the entire ruin of their business; and the greater part of our workmen, an end of their employment. A rupture with any of our neighbours upon the continent, though likely, too, to occasion some stop or interruption in the employments of some of all these different orders of people, is foreseen, however, without any such general emotion. The blood, of which the circulation is stopt in some of the smaller vessels, easily disgorges itself into the greater, without occasioning any dangerous disorder; but, when it is stopt in any of the greater vessels, convulsions, apoplexy, or death, are the immediate and unavoidable consequences. If but one of those overgrown manufactures, which, by means either of bounties or of the monopoly of the home and colony markets, have been artificially raised up to any unnatural height, finds some small stop or interruption in its employment, it frequently occasions a mutiny and disorder alarming to government, and embarrassing even to the deliberations of the legislature. How great, therefore, would be the disorder and confusion, it was thought, which must necessarily be occasioned by a sudden and entire stop in the employment of so great a proportion of our principal manufacturers?
