p131.zh: 此外,殖民地贸易的垄断通过迫使大不列颠的资本比自然会得到的资本大得多,似乎彻底打破了本来会在英国工业所有不同分支之间实现的自然平衡。 大不列颠的工业,不是适应许多小市场,而是主要适合一个大市场。 她的生意不是在很多小渠道经营,而是主要在一个大渠道经营。 但是,她的整个工业和商业体系因此变得不那么安全;她整个身体状态的健康状况不如本来那样健康。 在她目前的状况下,大不列颠类似于一些不健康的身体之一,其中某些重要部分生长过度,因此,它们可能发生许多危险失调,很少发生与所有部分分布更适当的事件。 在那个血流体中一小站,人为地膨胀,超出了自然范围,通过这个站点,我国工商业中一部分非自然部分被迫流通,极有可能给整个政治带来最危险的混乱。 因此,人们期望与殖民地决裂,对大不列颠人民的恐怖打击比他们对西班牙军舰或法国入侵的恐惧更大。 正是这种恐怖,无论是好还是不好,使废除印花行为在商人中至少成为一种流行的措施。 在完全被排斥在殖民地市场之外的情况下,是否只持续几年,我们大部分商人过去都希望他们预见到他们的贸易会完全停止;我们大部分的老制造商,他们的生意会完全被摧毁;我们更多的工人,他们的就业会结束。 然而,预计与我们大陆上的任何邻国发生破裂,虽然也有可能造成所有这些不同秩序中某些人的就业出现某种停止或中断,但却没有任何这种一般情绪。血液在某些较小的血管中被停止循环,很容易把自己分解为更大的血管,而不会引起任何危险的紊乱;但是,当血液在任何较大的血管中被停止时,抽搐、惊厥或死亡是直接和不可避免的后果。 如果只是其中一种过度生产的制成品,通过丰厚或垄断家庭和殖民地市场,被人为地提升到任何不自然的高度,在就业方面发现一些小的停工或中断,那么,它经常发生使政府感到震惊的兵变和混乱,甚至使立法机构的审议尴尬。 因此,人们认为,这种混乱和混乱将有多大,这必然是突然和完全停止雇用如此大比例的主要制造商造成的?

p132.original: Some moderate and gradual relaxation of the laws which give to Great Britain the exclusive trade to the colonies, till it is rendered in a great measure free, seems to be the only expedient which can, in all future times, deliver her from this danger; which can enable her, or even force her, to withdraw some part of her capital from this overgrown employment, and to turn it, though with less profit, towards other employments; and which, by gradually diminishing one branch of her industry, and gradually increasing all the rest, can, by degrees, restore all the different branches of it to that natural, healthful, and proper proportion, which perfect liberty necessarily establishes, and which perfect liberty can alone preserve. To open the colony trade all at once to all nations, might not only occasion some transitory inconveniency, but a great permanent loss, to the greater part of those whose industry or capital is at present engaged in it. The sudden loss of the employment, even of the ships which import the eighty-two thousand hogsheads of tobacco, which are over and above the consumption of Great Britain, might alone be felt very sensibly. Such are the unfortunate effects of all the regulations of the mercantile system. They not only introduce very dangerous disorders into the state of the body politic, but disorders which it is often difficult to remedy, without occasioning, for a time at least, still greater disorders. In what manner, therefore, the colony trade ought gradually to be opened; what are the restraints which ought first, and what are those which ought last, to be taken away; or in what manner the natural system of perfect liberty and justice ought gradually to be restored, we must leave to the wisdom of future statesmen and legislators to determine.
p132.zh: 给予大不列颠殖民地独有贸易的法律,在相当自由的情况下,有些适度和逐步的放松,似乎是今后所有时期能够使她摆脱这种危险的唯一办法;这可以使她,甚至迫使她,从这种过度增长的就业中撤出一部分资本,并将它,虽然利润较少,但转向其他就业;通过逐渐缩小其产业的一个分支,并逐步增加所有其他部分,可以在某种程度上将它的所有不同分支恢复到自然、健康和适当的比例,而完美自由必然能够确立,而且完美自由能够单独维护。立即向所有国家开放殖民地贸易,不仅可能给那些工业或资本目前从事这种贸易的大多数国家带来一些过渡性的不便,而且会造成极大的永久损失。突然失去工作,甚至进口八万二千头烟草的船舶,这些烟草超出了大不列颠的消费范围,也许仅能令人感到非常理智。 这就是商业系统所有规章的不幸后果。 它们不仅将非常危险的紊乱引入身体政治状态,而且往往难以补救的紊乱,至少一段时间没有发生,仍然更严重的紊乱。 因此,应该以何种方式逐步开放殖民地贸易;应该首先采取哪些限制措施,应该采取哪些最后限制措施,以何种方式逐步恢复完全自由和正义的自然制度,我们必须让未来的政治家和立法者的智慧来决定。

p133.original: Five different events, unforeseen and unthought of, have very fortunately concurred to hinder Great Britain from feeling, so sensibly as it was generally expected she would, the total exclusion which has now taken place for more than a year (from the first of December 1774) from a very important branch of the colony trade, that of the twelve associated provinces of North America. First, those colonies, in preparing themselves for their non-importation agreement, drained Great Britain completely of all the commodities which were fit for their market; secondly, the extra ordinary demand of the Spanish flota has, this year, drained Germany and the north of many commodities, linen in particular, which used to come into competition, even in the British market, with the manufactures of Great Britain; thirdly, the peace between Russia and Turkey has occasioned an extraordinary demand from the Turkey market, which, during the distress of the country, and while a Russian fleet was cruizing in the Archipelago, had been very poorly supplied; fourthly, the demand of the north of Europe for the manufactures of Great Britain has been increasing from year to year, for some time past; and, fifthly, the late partition, and consequential pacification of Poland, by opening the market of that great country, have, this year, added an extraordinary demand from thence to the increasing demand of the north. These events are all, except the fourth, in their nature transitory and accidental; and the exclusion from so important a branch of the colony trade, if unfortunately it should continue much longer, may still occasion some degree of distress. This distress, however, as it will come on gradually, will be felt much less severely than if it had come on all at once; and, in the mean time, the industry and capital of the country may find a new employment and direction, so as to prevent this distress from ever rising to any considerable height.
p133.zh: 5个不同事件,意外的和没有想到的,都非常幸运地同意阻碍大不列颠的感受,正如人们一般预期的那样,她现在(从1774年12月1日起)完全被排除在殖民地贸易的一个非常重要的分支,即北美12个相关省份之外。 首先,这些殖民地在准备其非进口协议时,完全消耗了大不列颠所有适合其市场商品;其次,西班牙船队的额外普通需求今年消耗了德国和北方许多商品,特别是亚麻,这些商品曾经与英国市场竞争,甚至与英国的制成品竞争;第三,俄罗斯和土耳其之间的和平引起了土耳其市场的异常需求,而土耳其市场在该国受困期间,俄罗斯船队在群岛上十字架时,供应非常差;第四,欧洲北部对大不列颠的制造的需求逐年逐年增长,过去一段时间;第五,波兰的后期分割和随后的绥靖,使该伟大国家的市场开放,使这一年从北方的需求增加。 除第四起外,这些事件都是暂时的和偶然的;将殖民地贸易的一个分支排除在如此重要的之外,如果不幸地继续下去,仍然可能带来一定程度的痛苦。 然而,随着这种痛苦将逐渐发生,人们将比一次一次发生的严重得多;在极短的时间内,我国的工业和资本可能找到新的就业和方向,以防止这种痛苦升级到任何相当高度。

p134.original: The monopoly of the colony trade, therefore, so far as it has turned towards that trade a greater proportion of the capital of Great Britain than what would otherwise have gone to it, has in all cases turned it, from a foreign trade of consumption with a neighbouring, into one with a more distant country; in many cases from a direct foreign trade of consumption into a round-about one; and, in some cases, from all foreign trade of consumption into a carrying trade. It has, in all cases, therefore, turned it from a direction in which it would have maintained a greater quantity of productive labour, into one in which it can maintain a much smaller quantity. By suiting, besides, to one particular market only, so great a part of the industry and commerce of Great Britain, it has rendered the whole state of that industry and commerce more precarious and less secure, than if their produce had been accommodated to a greater variety of markets.
p134.zh: 因此,殖民地贸易的垄断,由于它转向大不列颠的资本贸易比本来会流向它的比例要大,因此在所有情况下,它都从与邻国的对外消费贸易转变为与一个更远的国家的贸易;在许多情况下,从直接的对外消费贸易转变为环形贸易;在某些情况下,从所有对外消费贸易转变为承载贸易。 因此,在所有情况下,它都从本来可以维持更多生产性劳动力的方向转向能够维持数量少得多的生产性劳动力。 此外,它仅适合一个特定的市场,而这个市场是大不列颠工商业的一大部分,它使整个工业和商业状况更加不稳定和不安全,比如果它们的产品能够适应更多的市场。

p135.original: We must carefully distinguish between the effects of the colony trade and those of the monopoly of that trade. The former are always and necessarily beneficial; the latter always and necessarily hurtful. But the former are so beneficial, that the colony trade, though subject to a monopoly, and, notwithstanding the hurtful effects of that monopoly, is still, upon the whole, beneficial, and greatly beneficial, though a good deal less so than it otherwise would be.
p135.zh: 我们必须仔细区分殖民地贸易的影响和垄断殖民地贸易的影响。前者总是而且必然是有利的;后者总是而且必然是有害的。 但前者如此有利,以至于殖民地贸易尽管受到垄断,尽管这种垄断的有害影响,但总的来说仍然是有利和巨大的好处,尽管比其他情况要少很多。

p136.original: The effect of the colony trade, in its natural and free state, is to open a great though distant market, for such parts of the produce of British industry as may exceed the demand of the markets nearer home, of those of Europe, and of the countries which lie round the Mediterranean sea. In its natural and free state, the colony trade, without drawing from those markets any part of the produce which had ever been sent to them, encourages Great Britain to increase the surplus continually, by continually presenting new equivalents to be exchanged for it. In its natural and free state, the colony trade tends to increase the quantity of productive labour in Great Britain, but without altering in any respect the direction of that which had been employed there before. In the natural and free state of the colony trade, the competition of all other nations would hinder the rate of profit from rising above the common level, either in the new market, or in the new employment. The new market, without drawing any thing from the old one, would create, if one may say so, a new produce for its own supply; and that new produce would constitute a new capital for carrying on the new employment, which, in the same manner, would draw nothing from the old one.
p136.zh: 殖民地贸易在其自然和自由状态下,其作用是为英国工业产品中可能超过更邻近的市场、欧洲市场和地中海周边国家的需求的部分开辟一个巨大而遥远的市场。殖民地贸易在其自然和自由的状态下,不从这些市场提取曾经寄给它们的任何部分的农产品,就鼓励大不列颠不断增加盈余,不断提出新的等价物来换取盈余。 在自然和自由的状态下,殖民地贸易往往增加大不列颠的生产性劳动力数量,但丝毫不改变以前在那里就业的方向。 在殖民地贸易的自然和自由状态下,所有其他国家的竞争将妨碍利润率在新市场或新就业中超过共同水平。新的市场,不从旧市场中提取任何东西,如果人们可以这样说,将会为自己的供应创造新的产品;而新的产品将构成新的资本,用于继续新的就业,而以同样的方式,它不会从旧市场中提取任何东西。

p137.original: The monopoly of the colony trade, on the contrary, by excluding the competition of other nations, and thereby raising the rate of profit, both in the new market and in the new employment, draws produce from the old market, and capital from the old employment. To augment our share of the colony trade beyond what it otherwise would be, is the avowed purpose of the monopoly. If our share of that trade were to be no greater with, than it would have been without the monopoly, there could have been no reason for establishing the monopoly. But whatever forces into a branch of trade, of which the returns are slower and more distant than those of the greater part of other trades, a greater proportion of the capital of any country, than what of its own accord would go to that branch, necessarily renders the whole quantity of productive labour annually maintained there, the whole annual produce of the land and labour of that country, less than they otherwise would be. It keeps down the revenue of the inhabitants of that country below what it would naturally rise to, and thereby diminishes their power of accumulation. It not only hinders, at all times, their capital from maintaining so great a quantity of productive labour as it would otherwise maintain, but it hinders it from increasing so fast as it would otherwise increase, and, consequently, from maintaining a still greater quantity of productive labour.
p137.zh: 相反,殖民地贸易的垄断通过排除其他国家的竞争,从而在新市场和新就业中提高利润率,从旧市场中提取产品,从旧就业中提取资本。扩大我们在殖民地贸易中的份额,使其超出本来会达到的程度,是垄断的公开目的。 如果我们在这种贸易中的份额不会超过没有垄断的情况下的份额,那么就没有理由建立这种垄断。 但是,无论贸易分支的回报比其他贸易的大部分的回报慢、远,任何国家的资本比例都比它自己愿意向该分支提供多少,任何力量都必然使该国每年维持的全部生产性劳动力、其土地和劳动力的全部年度产量都比其他情况要少。 它使该国居民的收入低于它自然会达到的水平,从而削弱了他们的积累能力。 它不仅在任何时候都妨碍资本维持如此数量的生产劳动力,否则它会维持如此数量的生产劳动力,而且阻碍资本增长如此之快,否则还会增加,从而也阻碍资本维持更多生产劳动力。

p138.original: The natural good effects of the colony trade, however, more than counterbalance to Great Britain the bad effects of the monopoly; so that, monopoly and altogether, that trade, even as it is carried on at present, is not only advantageous, but greatly advantageous. The new market and the new employment which are opened by the colony trade, are of much greater extent than that portion of the old market and of the old employment which is lost by the monopoly. The new produce and the new capital which has been created, if one may say so, by the colony trade, maintain in Great Britain a greater quantity of productive labour than what can have been thrown out of employment by the revulsion of capital from other trades of which the returns are more frequent. If the colony trade, however, even as it is carried on at present, is advantageous to Great Britain, it is not by means of the monopoly, but in spite of the monopoly.
p138.zh: 然而,殖民地贸易的自然良好影响不仅仅是与大不列颠的制衡,还有垄断的坏影响;因此,垄断和整个贸易,即使目前仍在继续,不仅有利,而且非常有利。殖民地贸易所开辟的新市场和新就业远远大于旧市场和被垄断者失去的旧就业。殖民地贸易创造的新产品和新资本,如果可以这么说的话,在大不列颠维持的生产性劳动力数量超过了其他贸易资本的回流可能使就业丧失的数量,而其他贸易的回报却更为频繁。 但是,如果殖民地贸易,即使目前仍在进行,对大不列颠也有利,那么它不是通过垄断,而是尽管有垄断。

p139.original: It is rather for the manufactured than for the rude produce of Europe, that the colony trade opens a new market. Agriculture is the proper business of all new colonies; a business which the cheapness of land renders more advantageous than any other. They abound, therefore, in the rude produce of land; and instead of importing it from other countries, they have generally a large surplus to export. In new colonies, agriculture either draws hands from all other employments, or keeps them from going to any other employment. There are few hands to spare for the necessary, and none for the ornamental manufactures. The greater part of the manufactures of both kinds they find it cheaper to purchase of other countries than to make for themselves. It is chiefly by encouraging the manufactures of Europe, that the colony trade indirectly encourages its agriculture. The manufacturers of Europe, to whom that trade gives employment, constitute a new market for the produce of the land, and the most advantageous of all markets; the home market for the corn and cattle, for the bread and butcher's meat of Europe, is thus greatly extended by means of the trade to America.
p139.zh: 更何况是制造者而不是欧洲粗鲁的农产品,殖民地贸易打开了一个新的市场。农业是所有新殖民地的正当业务;由于土地便宜,这种业务比任何其他业务更有利。 因此,它们大量生产粗鲁的土地;它们不是从其他国家进口土地,而是一般有大量的剩余出口。 在新的殖民地,农业要么从所有其他就业中抽取手,要么阻止他们从事任何其他就业。没有什么手可以留作必要的物品,没有手可以做装饰品。 他们认为,这两种制造品中,购买其他国家比自己制造要便宜得多。殖民地贸易主要是通过鼓励欧洲的制造业,间接鼓励其农业。 欧洲的制造商,贸易为它们提供了就业机会,是土地生产的新市场,也是所有市场中最有利的市场;因此,通过向美国贸易,玉米和牛的家用市场,以及欧洲的面包和屠夫肉的家用市场大大扩展。

p140.original: But that the monopoly of the trade of populous and thriving colonies is not alone sufficient to establish, or even to maintain, manufactures in any country, the examples of Spain and Portugal sufficiently demonstrate. Spain and Portugal were manufacturing countries before they had any considerable colonies. Since they had the richest and most fertile in the world, they have both ceased to be so.
p140.zh: 但是,对人口众多和繁荣的殖民地贸易的垄断并不足以在任何国家建立甚至维持制成品,西班牙和葡萄牙的例子就足以证明这一点。 西班牙和葡萄牙在拥有任何相当的殖民地之前,都是制造国. 由于他们拥有世界上最富有和最肥沃的财富,所以他们都不再如此了。

p141.original: In Spain and Portugal, the bad effects of the monopoly, aggravated by other causes, have, perhaps, nearly overbalanced the natural good effects of the colony trade. These causes seem to be other monopolies of different kinds: the degradation of the value of gold and silver below what it is in most other countries; the exclusion from foreign markets by improper taxes upon exportation, and the narrowing of the home market, by still more improper taxes upon the transportation of goods from one part of the country to another; but above all, that irregular and partial administration of justice which often protects the rich and powerful debtor from the pursuit of his injured creditor, and which makes the industrious part of the nation afraid to prepare goods for the consumption of those haughty and great men, to whom they dare not refuse to sell upon credit, and from whom they are altogether uncertain of repayment.
p141.zh: 在西班牙和葡萄牙,由于其他原因而加剧的垄断的不良后果,也许几乎过度平衡了殖民地贸易的自然良好影响。 这些原因似乎是其他不同种类的垄断:黄金和白银的价值低于大多数其他国家的水平;出口税不适当,使本国市场被排斥在外国市场之外,对从该国一个地区向另一个地区运送货物征收更不适当的税;但最重要的是,不规则和部分的司法往往保护富强的债务人不受其受害债权人的追逐,使国家的勤奋部分不敢准备货物供那些傲慢和伟大的人消费,他们不敢拒绝通过信贷出售给这些人,他们完全不确定偿还。

p142.original: In England, on the contrary, the natural good effects of the colony trade, assisted by other causes, have in a great measure conquered the bad effects of the monopoly. These causes seem to be, the general liberty of trade, which, notwithstanding some restraints, is at least equal, perhaps superior, to what it is in any other country; the liberty of exporting, duty free, almost all sorts of goods which are the produce of domestic industry, to almost any foreign country; and what, perhaps, is of still greater importance, the unbounded liberty of transporting them from one part of our own country to any other, without being obliged to give any account to any public office, without being liable to question or examination of any kind; but, above all, that equal and impartial administration of justice, which renders the rights of the meanest British subject respectable to the greatest, and which, by securing to every man the fruits of his own industry, gives the greatest and most effectual encouragement to every sort of industry.
p142.zh: 相反,在英国,殖民地贸易的自然良好影响在其它原因的协助下,在很大程度上征服了垄断的恶劣影响. 这些原因似乎是:贸易的一般自由,尽管存在一些限制,但至少与任何其他国家的情况相同,也许更优越;出口、免税、几乎是国内工业产品的所有种类货物的自由,几乎是任何外国;将货物从我国某一地区运往任何其他国家,而不必对任何公职作出任何说明,而不受任何种类的质疑或检查,这种自由可能更为重要;但最重要的是,平等和公正的司法,使最卑鄙的英国人的权利受到最伟大的尊重,并且通过确保每个人自己工业的果实,使每一种工业都得到最大和最有效的鼓励。

p143.original: If the manufactures of Great Britain, however, have been advanced, as they certainly have, by the colony trade, it has not been by means of the monopoly of that trade, but in spite of the monopoly. The effect of the monopoly has been, not to augment the quantity, but to alter the quality and shape of a part of the manufactures of Great Britain, and to accommodate to a market, from which the returns are slow and distant, what would otherwise have been accommodated to one from which the returns are frequent and near. Its effect has consequently been, to turn a part of the capital of Great Britain from an employment in which it would have maintained a greater quantity of manufacturing industry, to one in which it maintains a much smaller, and thereby to diminish, instead of increasing, the whole quantity of manufacturing industry maintained in Great Britain.
p143.zh: 但是,如果大不列颠的制造业象殖民地贸易那样得到推进,那它不是通过垄断这种贸易,而是通过垄断。垄断的影响不是增加数量,而是改变大不列颠部分制成品的质量和形状,并适应一个市场,从中收益缓慢、遥远,否则本可以适应一个收益频繁和接近的市场。 因此,它的作用是,将大不列颠首都的一部分从本来可以维持更多制造业的就业转为维持更小的制造业,从而减少而不是增加大不列颠维持的全部制造业。

p144.original: The monopoly of the colony trade, therefore, like all the other mean and malignant expedients of the mercantile system, depresses the industry of all other countries, but chiefly that of the colonies, without in the least increasing, but on the contrary diminishing, that of the country in whose favour it is established.
p144.zh: 因此,殖民地贸易的垄断,同商贸制度所有其他的恶毒手段一样,抑制了所有其他国家的工业,但主要是殖民地的工业,没有至少增加,相反,减少的是它所建立的国家的工业。

p145.original: The monopoly hinders the capital of that country, whatever may, at any particular time, be the extent of that capital, from maintaining so great a quantity of productive labour as it would otherwise maintain, and from affording so great a revenue to the industrious inhabitants as it would otherwise afford. But as capital can be increased only by savings from revenue, the monopoly, by hindering it from affording so great a revenue as it would otherwise afford, necessarily hinders it from increasing so fast as it would otherwise increase, and consequently from maintaining a still greater quantity of productive labour, and affording a still greater revenue to the industrious inhabitants of that country. One great original source of revenue, therefore, the wages of labour, the monopoly must necessarily have rendered, at all times, less abundant than it otherwise would have been.
p145.zh: 垄断阻碍了该国的资本,无论在任何特定时间,无论这种资本有多大,都无法维持如此多的生产性劳动力,也无法为勤奋的居民提供如此丰厚的收入,否则,它会负担如此之多的收入。 但是,由于资本只能靠收入的储蓄来增加,垄断通过阻碍它支付如此之大的收入,必然妨碍它增加如此之快,否则就会增加,从而维持更多的生产性劳动力,使该国杰出的居民获得更多的收入。 因此,一个巨大的原始收入来源,即劳动工资,在任何时候都必须使垄断变得比本来要少。

p146.original: By raising the rate of mercantile profit, the monopoly discourages the improvement of land. The profit of improvement depends upon the difference between what the land actually produces, and what, by the application of a certain capital, it can be made to produce. If this difference affords a greater profit than what can be drawn from an equal capital in any mercantile employment, the improvement of land will draw capital from all mercantile employments. If the profit is less, mercantile employments will draw capital from the improvement of land. Whatever, therefore, raises the rate of mercantile profit, either lessens the superiority, or increases the inferiority of the profit of improvement: and, in the one case, hinders capital from going to improvement, and in the other draws capital from it; but by discouraging improvement, the monopoly necessarily retards the natural increase of another great original source of revenue, the rent of land. By raising the rate of profit, too, the monopoly necessarily keeps up the market rate of interest higher than it otherwise would be. But the price of land, in proportion to the rent which it affords, the number of years purchase which is commonly paid for it, necessarily falls as the rate of interest rises, and rises as the rate of interest falls. The monopoly, therefore, hurts the interest of the landlord two different ways, by retarding the natural increase, first, of his rent, and, secondly, of the price which he would get for his land, in proportion to the rent which it affords.
p146.zh: 通过提高商贸利润率,垄断阻碍了土地的改善.改良的利润取决于土地的实际生产量,以及利用一定资本能够生产多少之间的差别。 如果这种差别比任何商业就业中平等资本所能获取的利润要大,那么土地的改善将从所有商业就业中提取资本。 如果利润减少,商业就业将从改良土地中提取资本。 因此,无论如何提高商业利润率,要么降低优越性,要么提高改良利润的低劣程度:在一种情况下,阻碍资本走向改良,在另一种情况下,则从中提取资本;但是,通过阻止改良,垄断必然会阻碍另一个巨大的原始收入来源,即土地租金的自然增长。 通过提高利润率,垄断必然使市场利率高于其他市场利率。 但土地价格,按所付租金的比例,购买年数一般支付,必然随着利率的上升而下降,利率的下降而上升. 因此,垄断损害地主的利益有两种不同的方式,一是阻止自然增加租金,二是按租金的一定比例减少土地租金。

p147.original: The monopoly, indeed, raises the rate of mercantile profit and thereby augments somewhat the gain of our merchants. But as it obstructs the natural increase of capital, it tends rather to diminish than to increase the sum total of the revenue which the inhabitants of the country derive from the profits of stock; a small profit upon a great capital generally affording a greater revenue than a great profit upon a small one. The monopoly raises the rate of profit, but it hinders the sum of profit from rising so high as it otherwise would do.
p147.zh: 事实上,这种垄断提高了商业利润率,从而在一定程度上增加了我们商人的收益。 但是,由于它阻碍资本的自然增长,它往往减少而不是增加该国居民从股票利润中获得的收入总额;一个大资本的小额利润一般比一个小资本的巨额利润支付更多的收入。垄断会提高利润率,但是它会阻碍利润总额从高涨到高涨。

p148.original: All the original sources of revenue, the wages of labour, the rent of land, and the profits of stock, the monopoly renders much less abundant than they otherwise would be. To promote the little interest of one little order of men in one country, it hurts the interest of all other orders of men in that country, and of all the men in all other countries.
p148.zh: 所有原始的收入来源、劳动工资、土地租金和股票利润,垄断比其他的要少得多。 为了促进一个国家中一个小男人的一点兴趣,它伤害了这个国家中所有其他男人和所有其他国家所有男人的利益。

p149.original: It is solely by raising the ordinary rate of profit, that the monopoly either has proved, or could prove, advantageous to any one particular order of men. But besides all the bad effects to the country in general, which have already been mentioned as necessarily resulting from a higher rate of profit, there is one more fatal, perhaps, than all these put together, but which, if we may judge from experience, is inseparably connected with it. The high rate of profit seems everywhere to destroy that parsimony which, in other circumstances, is natural to the character of the merchant. When profits are high, that sober virtue seems to be superfluous, and expensive luxury to suit better the affluence of his situation. But the owners of the great mercantile capitals are necessarily the leaders and conductors of the whole industry of every nation; and their example has a much greater influence upon the manners of the whole industrious part of it than that of any other order of men. If his employer is attentive and parsimonious, the workman is very likely to be so too; but if the master is dissolute and disorderly, the servant, who shapes his work according to the pattern which his master prescribes to him, will shape his life, too, according to the example which he sets him. Accumulation is thus prevented in the hands of all those who are naturally the most disposed to accumulate; and the funds destined for the maintenance of productive labour, receive no augmentation from the revenue of those who ought naturally to augment them the most. The capital of the country, instead of increasing, gradually dwindles away, and the quantity of productive labour maintained in it grows every day less and less. Have the exorbitant profits of the merchants of Cadiz and Lisbon augmented the capital of Spain and Portugal? Have they alleviated the poverty, have they promoted the industry, of those two beggarly countries? Such has been the tone of mercantile expense in those two trading cities, that those exorbitant profits, far from augmenting the general capital of the country, seem scarce to have been sufficient to keep up the capitals upon which they were made. Foreign capitals are every day intruding themselves, if I may say so, more and more into the trade of Cadiz and Lisbon. It is to expel those foreign capitals from a trade which their own grows every day more and more insufficient for carrying on, that the Spaniards and Portuguese endeavour every day to straiten more and more the galling bands of their absurd monopoly. Compare the mercantile manners of Cadiz and Lisbon with those of Amsterdam, and you will be sensible how differently the conduct and character of merchants are affected by the high and by the low profits of stock. The merchants of London, indeed, have not yet generally become such magnificent lords as those of Cadiz and Lisbon; but neither are they in general such attetitive and parsimonious burghers as those of Amsterdam. They are supposed, however, many of them, to be a good deal richer than the greater part of the former, and not quire so rich as many of the latter: but the rate of their profit is commonly much lower than that of the former, and a good deal higher than that of the latter. Light come, light go, says the proverb; and the ordinary tone of expense seems everywhere to be regulated, not so much according to the real ability of spending, as to the supposed facility of getting money to spend.
p149.zh: 只有提高正常利润率,垄断才能证明或可能证明对某一个特定的男性秩序有利。 但是,除了已经提到必然因利润率提高而给整个国家带来的所有不利影响之外,也许还有一种致命性,比所有这些影响加在一起还要严重,但是,如果我们从经验中作出判断,这种影响是不可分割的。高利润率似乎在任何地方都摧毁了这种陈情,在其他情况下,这种陈情是商人的自然特征。 当利润高的时候,这种清醒的美德似乎是多余的,而昂贵的奢侈品更适合他的处境富裕. 但是,大商贸首都的主人必然是每个国家整个工业的领导者和指挥者;他们的榜样对整个杰出部分的礼仪的影响远大于任何其他阶层的人。 如果雇主细心细心地对待他,那工人很可能也是这样;如果主人意志消沉,秩序混乱,那么仆人,按照主人向他规定的规律塑造他的作品,也会按照他树立的榜样来塑造他的生活. 因此,所有自然最愿意积累的人都无法积累;而用于维持生产性劳动力的资金,则不会从那些自然而然地最应该增加其收入的人的收入中获得任何增加。国家首都不但没有增加,反而逐渐萎缩,所维持的生产性劳动力数量日增日减. 加的斯和里斯本商人的巨额利润是否增加了西班牙和葡萄牙的首都? 他们是否缓解了这两个乞丐国家的贫穷,是否促进了工业? 这两个贸易城市的商贸支出的基调就是,这些高额利润远远没有增加该国的总资本,似乎不足以维持其资本的形成。外国首都每天都在干涉自己,如果我可以这样说的话,它们越来越多地介入加的斯和里斯本的贸易。 西班牙人和葡萄牙人每天都在努力使其荒谬的垄断集团日益紧张,正是为了将外国首都从它们自己日复一日地增长、越来越不足以继续的贸易中驱逐出来。将卡迪兹和里斯本的商贸礼仪与阿姆斯特丹的礼仪相比较,你将明智地看到,股票的高利润和低利润对商人的行为和品格的影响如何不同。 事实上,伦敦的商人还没有像卡迪兹和里斯本的商人那样普遍成为如此雄伟的领主;但是,他们也没有像阿姆斯特丹的商人那样一般地如此有节制和刻薄的堡垒. 然而,他们中许多人应该比前者更富有,而不是像后者那样富有:但他们的利润率通常比前者低得多,而且比后者高得多。光来,光去,说着谚语;而普通的费用基调似乎到处都受到管制,而不是根据实际的支出能力,到所谓的获得资金来花钱的便利.

p150.original: It is thus that the single advantage which the monopoly procures to a single order of men, is in many different ways hurtful to the general interest of the country.
p150.zh: 因此,垄断给男子的单一秩序带来的单一优势在许多不同方面损害国家的普遍利益。

p151.original: To found a great empire for the sole purpose of raising up a people of customers, may at first sight, appear a project fit only for a nation of shopkeepers. It is, however, a project altogether unfit for a nation of shopkeepers, but extremely fit for a nation whose government is influenced by shopkeepers. Such statesmen, and such statesmen only, are capable of fancying that they will find some advantage in employing the blood and treasure of their fellow-citizens, to found and maintain such an empire. Say to a shopkeeper, Buy me a good estate, and I shall always buy my clothes at your shop, even though I should pay somewhat dearer than what I can have them for at other shops; and you will not find him very forward to embrace your proposal. But should any other person buy you such an estate, the shopkeeper will be much obliged to your benefactor if he would enjoin you to buy all your clothes at his shop. England purchased for some of her subjects, who found themselves uneasy at home, a great estate in a distant country. The price, indeed, was very small, and instead of thirty years purchase, the ordinary price of land in the present times, it amounted to little more than the expense of the different equipments which made the first discovery, reconnoitered the coast, and took a fictitious possession of the country. The land was good, and of great extent; and the cultivators having plenty of good ground to work upon, and being for some time at liberty to sell their produce where they pleased, became, in the course of little more than thirty or forty years (between 1620 and 1660), so numerous and thriving a people, that the shopkeepers and other traders of England wished to secure to themselves the monopoly of their custom. Without pretending, therefore, that they had paid any part, either of the original purchase money, or of the subsequent expense of improvement, they petitioned the parliament, that the cultivators of America might for the future be confined to their shop; first, for buying all the goods which they wanted from Europe; and, secondly, for selling all such parts of their own produce as those traders might find it convenient to buy. For they did not find it convenient to buy every part of it. Some parts of it imported into England, might have interfered with some of the trades which they themselves carried on at home. Those particular parts of it, therefore, they were willing that the colonists should sell where they could; the farther off the better; and upon that account proposed that their market should be confined to the countries south of Cape Finisterre. A clause in the famous act of navigation established this truly shopkeeper proposal into a law.
p151.zh: 为了养大一个有顾客的民族而建立一个伟大的帝国,乍一看,它可能看起来是一个只适合一个店主国家的项目。 然而,这个项目完全不适合一个有店主的国家,但极适合一个政府受到店主影响的国家。 这些政治家,也只有这些政治家,能够幻想他们在利用同胞的血液和财富方面会找到一些优势,找到并维持这样一个帝国. 对一个店主说,给我买个好庄园,我总是会在你的店里买我的衣服,尽管我应该支付比其他店铺买得多一些的钱;你不会发现他非常热衷于接受你的求婚。 但是如果有其他人给你买这种地产 店主会非常感激你的恩人 如果他会命令你 在他的店里买你所有的衣服英格兰为她的一些臣民购买了,他们发现自己在家中感到不自在,在一个遥远的国家中,一个伟大的庄园.价格确实非常小,现在土地的普通价格不是30年的购买,而只是第一次发现、侦察海岸、虚构地占有国家的不同设备的费用。这片土地是好的,而且在很大程度上是好的;种植者有充足的良田可以工作,在他们愿意的地方有一段时间可以自由地出售他们的农产品,在短短三四十年的时间里(1620年到1660年之间),他们变得如此众多和兴旺,以至于英格兰的店主和其他商人都希望确保自己能够垄断他们的习俗。 因此,他们没有假装支付了任何一部分,无论是原购货款,还是后来的改良费用,他们向议会请愿,要求美国种植者今后可能只许到他们的商店去;第一,购买他们想要从欧洲购买的所有货物;第二,出售他们自己产品的所有部分,因为那些贸易商可能认为购买是方便的。 他们觉得买下它的每一部分并不方便。一部分进口到英国,可能干扰了他们自己在国内从事的一些贸易。 因此,他们愿意让殖民者在他们能够出售的地方出售这些特定部分,而且情况越好,因此,他们建议,他们的市场应限于菲尼斯特尔角以南的国家。著名的航海行为中有一条条款将这个真正的店主建议确立为法律.

p152.original: The maintenance of this monopoly has hitherto been the principal, or more properly, perhaps, the sole end and purpose of the dominion which Great Britain assumes over her colonies. In the exclusive trade, it is supposed, consists the great advantage of provinces, which have never yet afforded either revenue or military force for the support of the civil government, or the defence of the mother country. The monopoly is the principal badge of their dependency, and it is the sole fruit which has hitherto been gathered from that dependency. Whatever expense Great Britain has hitherto laid out in maintaining this dependency, has really been laid out in order to support this monopoly. The expense of the ordinary peace establishment of the colonies amounted, before the commencement of the present disturbances to the pay of twenty regiments of foot; to the expense of the artillery, stores, and extraordinary provisions, with which it was necessary to supply them; and to the expense of a very considerable naval force, which was constantly kept up, in order to guard from the smuggling vessels of other nations, the immense coast of North America, and that of our West Indian islands. The whole expense of this peace establishment was a charge upon the revenue of Great Britain, and was, at the same time, the smallest part of what the dominion of the colonies has cost the mother country. If we would know the amount of the whole, we must add to the annual expense of this peace establishment, the interest of the sums which, in consequence of their considering her colonies as provinces subject to her dominion, Great Britain has, upon different occasions, laid out upon their defence. We must add to it, in particular, the whole expense of the late war, and a great part of that of the war which preceded it. The late war was altogether a colony quarrel; and the whole expense of it, in whatever part of the world it might have been laid out, whether in Germany or the East Indies, ought justly to be stated to the account of the colonies. It amounted to more than ninety millions sterling, including not only the new debt which was contracted, but the two shillings in the pound additional land tax, and the sums which were every year borrowed from the sinking fund. The Spanish war which began in 1739 was principally a colony quarrel. Its principal object was to prevent the search of the colony ships, which carried on a contraband trade with the Spanish Main. This whole expense is, in reality, a bounty which has been given in order to support a monopoly. The pretended purpose of it was to encourage the manufactures, and to increase the commerce of Great Britain. But its real effect has been to raise the rate of mercantile profit, and to enable our merchants to turn into a branch of trade, of which the returns are more slow and distant than those of the greater part of other trades, a greater proportion of their capital than they otherwise would have done; two events which, if a bounty could have prevented, it might perhaps have been very well worth while to give such a bounty.
p152.zh: 维持这种垄断至今一直是大不列颠对其殖民地的统治权的主要,或更恰当,也许也是其唯一目的。 在专营贸易中,它应该包括各省的巨大优势,它们从未给予收入或军事力量支持文官政府,或保卫祖国.垄断是它们依赖的主要标志,也是迄今从这种依赖中收集的唯一成果。英国在维持这种依赖性方面迄今规定的任何开支,都是为了支持这种垄断而真正规定的。 在目前动乱开始之前,殖民地的普通和平建立费用相当于20个团的足费;炮兵、仓库和特别物资的费用,这是提供这些物资所必须的;以及一支相当庞大的海军部队的费用,为了防止其他国家走私船只、北美的庞大海岸和我们西印度岛屿的走私船只不断被扣留。这笔和平建设的全部费用是向大不列颠的收入收取的,同时也是殖民地的统治对祖国造成的损失中最小的一部分。 如果我们知道整个数额,我们就必须增加这一和平机构的每年开支,即大不列颠在不同的场合为捍卫和平而提出作为受她管辖的省份的殖民地而给予的利息。特别是,我们必须增加战争后期的全部开支,以及战争前的很大一部分开支。战争的后期完全是殖民地争吵;无论在世界任何地区,无论是在德国还是在东印度群岛,其全部开支都应该向殖民地的帐户说明。 它达9 000万英镑以上,不仅包括合同的新债务,还包括英镑附加土地税中的两先令,以及每年从沉没基金借款的数额。1739年开始的西班牙战争主要是殖民地争吵.其主要目的是防止搜查与西班牙主船进行违禁贸易的殖民地船只。 实际上,这笔费用是一笔赏金,是用来支持垄断的。其伪装的目的是鼓励制造,增加大不列颠的商业. 但是,它的真正效果是提高了商贸利润率,使我们的商人能够变成一个贸易分支,其回报比其他贸易的大部分的回报更缓慢,也更遥远,比他们本来会做的更多;两个事件,如果一笔赏金可以阻止,或许在给予这种赏金的同时,是十分值得的.

p153.original: Under the present system of management, therefore, Great Britain derives nothing but loss from the dominion which she assumes over her colonies.
p153.zh: 因此,在目前的管理制度下,大不列颠只能从她对其殖民地的统治权中得益。

p154.original: To propose that Great Britain should voluntarily give up all authority over her colonies, and leave them to elect their own magistrates, to enact their own laws, and to make peace and war, as they might think proper, would be to propose such a measure as never was, and never will be, adopted by any nation in the world. No nation ever voluntarily gave up the dominion of any province, how troublesome soever it might be to govern it, and how small soever the revenue which it afforded might be in proportion to the expense which it occasioned. Such sacrifices, though they might frequently be agreeable to the interest, are always mortifying to the pride of every nation; and, what is perhaps of still greater consequence, they are always contrary to the private interest of the governing part of it, who would thereby be deprived of the disposal of many places of trust and profit, of many opportunities of acquiring wealth and distinction, which the possession of the most turbulent, and, to the great body of the people, the most unprofitable province, seldom fails to afford. The most visionary enthusiasts would scarce be capable of proposing such a measure, with any serious hopes at least of its ever being adopted. If it was adopted, however, Great Britain would not only be immediately freed from the whole annual expense of the peace establishment of the colonies, but might settle with them such a treaty of commerce as would effectually secure to her a free trade, more advantageous to the great body of the people, though less so to the merchants, than the monopoly which she at present enjoys. By thus parting good friends, the natural affection of the colonies to the mother country, which, perhaps, our late dissensions have well nigh extinguished, would quickly revive. It might dispose them not only to respect, for whole centuries together, that treaty of commerce which they had concluded with us at parting, but to favour us in war as well as in trade, and instead of turbulent and factious subjects, to become our most faithful, affectionate, and generous allies; and the same sort of parental affection on the one side, and filial respect on the other, might revive between Great Britain and her colonies, which used to subsist between those of ancient Greece and the mother city from which they descended.
p154.zh: 建议英国自愿放弃对其殖民地的一切权力,让他们选举自己的地方法官,颁布自己的法律,并按他们可能认为适当的方式建立和平与战争,就是提出这样一个措施,世界上任何国家从来没有而且永远不会通过。没有任何一个国家会自愿放弃任何省份的统治权,不管管理它多么麻烦,它所提供的收入与它所花费的费用的比例多么小。 这种牺牲虽然常常符合利益,但总是使每个国家的骄傲蒙羞;也许后果更大的是,这种牺牲总是违背其管理部分的私人利益,从而剥夺了许多信任和利润场所的支配权,剥夺了许多获得财富和区别的机会,而最动荡的人拥有这种财富和区别,而对于伟大的人民来说,最无利可图的省份,却很少无法负担。 最有远见的爱好者很少能够提出这种措施,至少对它获得通过抱有任何严肃的希望。 但是,如果通过这项条约,大不列颠不仅将立即从建立殖民地的全部年度开支中解放出来,而且可能同它们达成这样的商业条约,从而实际上使她能够进行自由贸易,对广大人民更加有利,尽管对商人来说却比她目前享有的垄断要少。殖民地对祖国的自然感情,也许已经消亡了 我们的迟钝情绪,很快会恢复这样做不仅是为了共同尊重他们与我们共同缔结的商业条约,而且是为了在战争和贸易中偏袒我们,而不是动荡和现实的臣民,而是为了成为我们最忠实、最亲切和最慷慨的盟友;同样亲情和孝敬一方,可能使英国与她的殖民地之间复活,而后者曾经在古希腊的殖民地和他们所从来的母城之间生存。

p155.original: In order to render any province advantageous to the empire to which it belongs, it ought to afford, in time of peace, a revenue to the public, sufficient not only for defraying the whole expense of its own peace establishment, but for contributing its proportion to the support of the general government of the empire. Every province necessarily contributes, more or less, to increase the expense of that general government. If any particular province, therefore, does not contribute its share towards defraying this expense, an unequal burden must be thrown upon some other part of the empire. The extraordinary revenue, too, which every province affords to the public in time of war, ought, from parity of reason, to bear the same proportion to the extraordinary revenue of the whole empire, which its ordinary revenue does in time of peace. That neither the ordinary nor extraordinary revenue which Great Britain derives from her colonies, bears this proportion to the whole revenue of the British empire, will readily be allowed. The monopoly, it has been supposed, indeed, by increasing the private revenue of the people of Great Britain, and thereby enabling them to pay greater taxes, compensates the deficiency of the public revenue of the colonies. But this monopoly, I have endeavoured to show, though a very grievous tax upon the colonies, and though it may increase the revenue of a particular order of men in Great Britain, diminishes, instead of increasing, that of the great body of the people, and consequently diminishes, instead of increasing, the ability of the great body of the people to pay taxes. The men, too, whose revenue the monopoly increases, constitute a particular order, which it is both absolutely impossible to tax beyond the proportion of other orders, and extremely impolitic even to attempt to tax beyond that proportion, as I shall endeavour to show in the following book. No particular resource, therefore, can be drawn from this particular order.
p155.zh: 为了使任何省份对其所属的帝国有利,在和平时期,它应该为公众提供一笔收入,不仅足以支付它自己建立和平的全部费用,而且足以为帝国总政府的支持贡献它的比例。 每个省都一定多少为增加该总政府的费用作出贡献。 因此,如果任何特定省份不为支付这笔费用而贡献其份额,就必须将不平等的负担推向帝国的其他一些部分。 每个省份在战时都向公众提供特别收入,从合理角度讲,应承担整个帝国特别收入的同样比例,而其普通收入在和平时期就是如此。 大不列颠从其殖民地获得的普通或特殊收入,都无法轻易地占大英帝国全部收入的这个比例。垄断,实际上,是因为它增加了大不列颠人民的私人收入,从而使他们能够支付更大的税收,弥补了殖民地公共收入的不足。 但是,这种垄断,我努力表明,虽然对殖民地征收了非常沉重的税,虽然它可能增加大不列颠某一阶层人的收入,但是却削弱了而不是增加了人民伟大身体的收入,从而削弱了而不是增加了人民伟大身体的纳税能力。其收入增加的男子也构成了一种特别的秩序,既无法超过其他命令的比例征税,又极不礼貌,甚至试图超过这个比例征税,我将努力在下面的书中说明这一点。 因此,不能从这一特定顺序中提取任何特定资源。

p156.original: The colonies may be taxed either by their own assemblies, or by the parliament of Great Britain.
p156.zh: 殖民地可以由自己的议会征税,也可以由大不列颠议会征税.

p157.original: That the colony assemblies can never be so managed as to levy upon their constituents a public revenue, sufficient, not only to maintain at all times their own civil and military establishment, but to pay their proper proportion of the expense of the general government of the British empire, seems not very probable. It was a long time before even the parliament of England, though placed immediately under the eye of the sovereign, could be brought under such a system of management, or could be rendered sufficiently liberal in their grants for supporting the civil and military establishments even of their own country. It was only by distributing among the particular members of parliament a great part either of the offices, or of the disposal of the offices arising from this civil and military establishment, that such a system of management could be established, even with regard to the parliament of England. But the distance of the colony assemblies from the eye of the sovereign, their number, their dispersed situation, and their various constitutions, would render it very difficult to manage them in the same manner, even though the sovereign had the same means of doing it; and those means are wanting. It would be absolutely impossible to distribute among all the leading members of all the colony assemblies such a share, either of the offices, or of the disposal of the offices, arising from the general government of the British empire, as to dispose them to give up their popularity at home, and to tax their constituents for the support of that general government, of which almost the whole emoluments were to be divided among people who were strangers to them. The unavoidable ignorance of administration, besides, concerning the relative importance of the different members of those different assemblies, the offences which must frequently be given, the blunders which must constantly be committed, in attempting to manage them in this manner, seems to render such a system of management altogether impracticable with regard to them.
p157.zh: 殖民地议会永远无法管理到向选民征收足够的公共收入,不仅在任何时候都维持其自己的民事和军事机构,而且支付其适当比例的大英帝国总政府的费用,这似乎并不十分可能。英格兰议会虽然直接置于君主的眼中,但早就可以置于这种管理制度之下,或者在给予支持甚至其本国的民事和军事机构的赠款方面可以充分自由。 只有向议会特定成员分配大部分办公室,或处置这一民事和军事机构产生的办公室,才能建立这种管理制度,即使是英格兰议会也是如此。 但是,殖民地议会与君主视线的距离、数量、分散状况和各种宪法,即使君主拥有同样手段,也很难以同样方式管理它们;这些手段是缺乏的。绝对不可能在所有殖民地议会的主要成员中分配来自大英帝国总政府的这种份额,无论是办公室,还是办公室的处置,以便他们放弃在家中的受欢迎地位,并为支持该总政府而向选民征税,而该总政府几乎将全部薪酬分给对他们陌生的人。 此外,对于这些不同议会不同成员相对重要性的不可避免的无知,以及必须经常给予的罪行,以及为了以这种方式管理它们而必须不断犯下的错误,似乎使这种管理制度完全不可行。

p158.original: The colony assemblies, besides, cannot be supposed the proper judges of what is necessary for the defence and support of the whole empire. The care of that defence and support is not entrusted to them. It is not their business, and they have no regular means of information concerning it. The assembly of a province, like the vestry of a parish, may judge very properly concerning the affairs of its own particular district, but can have no proper means of judging concerning those of the whole empire. It cannot even judge properly concerning the proportion which its own province bears to the whole empire, or concerning the relative degree of its wealth and importance, compared with the other provinces; because those other provinces are not under the inspection and superintendency of the assembly of a particular province. What is necessary for the defence and support of the whole empire, and in what proportion each part ought to contribute, can be judged of only by that assembly which inspects and super-intends the affairs of the whole empire.
p158.zh: 此外,殖民地议会不能被认为是捍卫和支持整个帝国所必须的适当法官。 他们不负责辩护和支持。 这不关他们的事,他们没有经常的相关信息手段。 一个省的议会,如一个教区,可以非常恰当地判断它自己特定地区的事务,但不能适当地判断整个帝国的事务。 它甚至不能正确判断它自己的省份对整个帝国所占的份额,也不能判断它与其他省份相比的财富和重要性的相对程度;因为其他省份不受某一省份议会的检查和支配。保卫和支持整个帝国所必须的,以及每个部分应贡献多少比例,只能由检查和超度地影响整个帝国事务的大会来判断。

p159.original: It has been proposed, accordingly, that the colonies should be taxed by requisition, the parliament of Great Britain determining the sum which each colony ought to pay, and the provincial assembly assessing and levying it in the way that suited best the circumstances of the province. What concerned the whole empire would in this way be determined by the assembly which inspects and superintends the affairs of the whole empire; and the provincial affairs of each colony might still be regulated by its own assembly. Though the colonies should, in this case, have no representatives in the British parliament, yet, if we may judge by experience, there is no probability that the parliamentary requisition would be unreasonable. The parliament of England has not, upon any occasion, shewn the smallest disposition to overburden those parts of the empire which are not represented in parliament. The islands of Guernsey and Jersey, without any means of resisting the authority of parliament, are more lightly taxed than any part of Great Britain. Parliament, in attempting to exercise its supposed right, whether well or ill grounded, of taxing the colonies, has never hitherto demanded of them anything which even approached to a just proportion to what was paid by their fellow subjects at home. If the contribution of the colonies, besides, was to rise or fall in proportion to the rise or fall of the land-tax, parliament could not tax them without taxing, at the same time, its own constituents, and the colonies might, in this case, be considered as virtually represented in parliament.
p159.zh: 因此,有人建议,殖民地应征收征用税,由大不列颠议会确定每个殖民地应缴纳的金额,由省议会以最适合该省情况的方式进行评估和征收。有关整个帝国的事务,将以这种方式由检查和支配整个帝国事务的大会决定;每个殖民地的省事务仍可能由自己的大会管理。 虽然殖民地在此情况下不应在英国议会中有代表,但是,如果我们可以根据经验来判断,议会的征用不可能是不合理的.英格兰议会在任何时候都没有表现出最小的意向,要给帝国中那些没有在议会中代表的地方造成负担过重。根西岛和泽西岛没有任何手段抵抗议会的权威,因此比大不列颠的任何地方都更轻税.议会试图行使其对殖民地征税的所谓权利,无论是好还是不好,但迄今为止从未要求它们采取任何行动,甚至接近于其同胞在国内所付费用的公平比例。 此外,如果殖民地的贡献与土地税的增减成正比,议会不能不同时对自己的选民征税就对殖民地征税,在此情况下,殖民地可能被视为实际上在议会中的代表.

p160.original: Examples are not wanting of empires in which all the different provinces are not taxed, if I may be allowed the expression, in one mass; but in which the sovereign regulates the sum which each province ought to pay, and in some provinces assesses and levies it as he thinks proper; while in others he leaves it to be assessed and levied as the respective states of each province shall determine. In some provinces of France, the king not only imposes what taxes he thinks proper, but assesses and levies them in the way he thinks proper. From others he demands a certain sum, but leaves it to the states of each province to assess and levy that sum as they think proper. According to the scheme of taxing by requisition, the parliament of Great Britain would stand nearly in the same situation towards the colony assemblies, as the king of France does towards the states of those provinces which still enjoy the privilege of having states of their own, the provinces of France which are supposed to be the best governed.
p160.zh: 如果允许我用一个批量的表示,所有不同省份都不征税的帝国并不缺;但主权国规定每个省份应该支付的总和,有些省份则按他认为合适的方式进行评估和征税;而在另一些省份,他则按每个省份各自的州的决定,将它留给评估和征收。 在法国的一些省份,国王不仅强制征收他认为适当的税项,而且按照他认为合适的方式评估和征收. 他从其他人那里要求一定的金额,但让各省的各州按他们认为适当的方式评估和征收这笔金额。 根据征用征税办法,大不列颠议会对殖民地议会的情况几乎相同,法国国王对那些仍然享有拥有自己国家特权的省份,即法国本应治理最优的省份,采取同样的做法。

p161.original: But though, according to this scheme, the colonies could have no just reason to fear that their share of the public burdens should ever exceed the proper proportion to that of their fellow-citizens at home, Great Britain might have just reason to fear that it never would amount to that proper proportion. The parliament of Great Britain has not, for some time past, had the same established authority in the colonies, which the French king has in those provinces of France which still enjoy the privilege of having states of their own. The colony assemblies, if they were not very favourably disposed (and unless more skilfully managed than they ever have been hitherto, they are not very likely to be so), might still find many pretences for evading or rejecting the most reasonable requisitions of parliament. A French war breaks out, we shall suppose; ten millions must immediately be raised, in order to defend the seat of the empire. This sum must be borrowed upon the credit of some parliamentary fund mortgaged for paying the interest. Part of this fund parliament proposes to raise by a tax to be levied in Great Britain; and part of it by a requisition to all the different colony assemblies of America and the West Indies. Would people readily advance their money upon the credit of a fund which partly depended upon the good humour of all those assemblies, far distant from the seat of the war, and sometimes, perhaps, thinking themselves not much concerned in the event of it? Upon such a fund, no more money would probably be advanced than what the tax to be levied in Great Britain might be supposed to answer for. The whole burden of the debt contracted on account of the war would in this manner fall, as it always has done hitherto, upon Great Britain; upon a part of the empire, and not upon the whole empire. Great Britain is, perhaps, since the world began, the only state which, as it has extended its empire, has only increased its expense, without once augmenting its resources. Other states have generally disburdened themselves, upon their subject and subordinate provinces, of the most considerable part of the expense of defending the empire. Great Britain has hitherto suffered her subject and subordinate provinces to disburden themselves upon her of almost this whole expense. In order to put Great Britain upon a footing of equality with her own colonies, which the law has hitherto supposed to be subject and subordinate, it seems necessary, upon the scheme of taxing them by parliamentary requisition, that parliament should have some means of rendering its requisitions immediately effectual, in case the colony assemblies should attempt to evade or reject them; and what those means are, it is not very easy to conceive, and it has not yet been explained.
p161.zh: 但是,虽然根据这个计划,殖民地没有正当理由担心自己在公共负担中所占的份额永远超过本国同胞的恰当比例,但大不列颠也许有正当理由担心这永远不会达到适当比例. 大不列颠议会在过去一段时间里在殖民地中并没有同样的既定权威,法国国王在法国那些仍然享有拥有自己国家的特权的省份中也有这种权威.殖民地议会如果没有得到非常有利的处理(除非比以往更熟练地管理起来,它们不太可能如此),仍然可能发现许多借口可以逃避或拒绝议会最合理的要求。一场法国战争爆发了,我们假设;为了保卫帝国的席位,必须立即筹集一千万.这笔钱必须借入一些为支付利息而抵押的议会基金。 这一基金的一部分议会提议在大不列颠征收税费;一部分则向美洲和西印度群岛所有不同的殖民地议会征收税费。 人们是否愿意依靠一个基金的信用来预付资金,该基金部分依赖于远离战争所在地的所有这些议会的幽默,有时甚至认为在发生战争时自己并不十分关心?有了这样一个基金,可能不会比在大不列颠征收的税额多多少少。战争造成的全部债务负担将象以往那样,落在大不列颠身上;落在帝国的一部分,而不是整个帝国身上。 或许,自世界开始以来,大不列颠是唯一一个国家,因为它扩大了它的帝国,只增加了它的开支,而没有一次增加它的资源。其他国家一般都把保卫帝国的绝大部分费用从他们的属下和属下省份上推卸下来。 大不列颠迄今一直遭受着她的臣民和下级省份的折磨,使她几乎承受了这笔费用。 为了使大不列颠与她自己的殖民地处于平等的地位,而法律迄今一直应该对其适用和从属地位,根据议会征收的税收计划,看来有必要使议会拥有一些手段,使其征用立即生效,以防殖民地议会试图逃避或拒绝这些手段;这些手段是什么,很难设想,目前还没有解释。

p162.original: Should the parliament of Great Britain, at the same time, be ever fully established in the right of taxing the colonies, even independent of the consent of their own assemblies, the importance of those assemblies would, from that moment, be at an end, and with it, that of all the leading men of British America. Men desire to have some share in the management of public affairs, chiefly on account of the importance which it gives them. Upon the power which the greater part of the leading men, the natural aristocracy of every country, have of preserving or defending their respective importance, depends the stability and duration of every system of free government. In the attacks which those leading men are continually making upon the importance of one another, and in the defence of their own, consists the whole play of domestic faction and ambition. The leading men of America, like those of all other countries, desire to preserve their own importance. They feel, or imagine, that if their assemblies, which they are fond of calling parliaments, and of considering as equal in authority to the parliament of Great Britain, should be so far degraded as to become the humble ministers and executive officers of that parliament, the greater part of their own importance would be at an end. They have rejected, therefore, the proposal of being taxed by parliamentary requisition, and, like other ambitious and high-spirited men, have rather chosen to draw the sword in defence of their own importance.
p162.zh: 如果大不列颠的议会同时在对殖民地征税的权利上得到充分确立,甚至不受自己议会的同意,那么从那时起,这些议会的重要性将处于一个结束,并随之成为英美所有领导人物的结束。男子希望参与公共事务的管理,这主要是因为它给予他们的重要性。大部分领导者,每个国家的自然贵族,拥有维护或捍卫各自重要性的权力,取决于每个自由政府制度的稳定性和持续时间。 这些领导者不断攻击彼此的重要性,为了保卫自己,他们把国内派别和野心都包括进来。 美国的男主角,像所有其他国家的男主角一样,都希望保持他们自己的重要性. 他们感到或想象,如果他们的议会喜欢召集议会,并且认为与大不列颠议会具有同等权力,那么,如果这些议会被贬低,成为该议会的谦卑的部长和执行官员,那么,它们本身重要性的更大部分就到了尾声。 因此,他们拒绝了议会征用税的建议,并且与其他野心勃勃和高志强的人一样,选择拔剑来捍卫他们自己的重要性。

p163.original: Towards the declension of the Roman republic, the allies of Rome, who had borne the principal burden of defending the state and extending the empire, demanded to be admitted to all the privileges of Roman citizens. Upon being refused, the social war broke out. During the course of that war, Rome granted those privileges to the greater part of them, one by one, and in proportion as they detached themselves from the general confederacy. The parliament of Great Britain insists upon taxing the colonies; and they refuse to be taxed by a parliament in which they are not represented. If to each colony which should detach itself from the general confederacy, Great Britain should allow such a number of representatives as suited the proportion of what it contributed to the public revenue of the empire, in consequence of its being subjected to the same taxes, and in compensation admitted to the same freedom of trade with its fellow-subjects at home; the number of its representatives to be augmented as the proportion of its contribution might afterwards augment; a new method of acquiring importance, a new and more dazzling object of ambition, would be presented to the leading men of each colony. Instead of piddling for the little prizes which are to be found in what may be called the paltry raffle of colony faction, they might then hope, from the presumption which men naturally have in their own ability and good fortune, to draw some of the great prizes which sometimes come from the wheel of the great state lottery of British politics. Unless this or some other method is fallen upon, and there seems to be none more obvious than this, of preserving the importance and of gratifying the ambition of the leading men of America, it is not very probable that they will ever voluntarily submit to us; and we ought to consider, that the blood which must be shed in forcing them to do so, is, every drop of it, the blood either of those who are, or of those whom we wish to have for our fellow citizens. They are very weak who flatter themselves that, in the state to which things have come, our colonies will be easily conquered by force alone. The persons who now govern the resolutions of what they call their continental congress, feel in themselves at this moment a degree of importance which, perhaps, the greatest subjects in Europe scarce feel. From shopkeepers, trades men, and attorneys, they are become statesmen and legislators, and are employed in contriving a new form of government for an extensive empire, which, they flatter themselves, will become, and which, indeed, seems very likely to become, one of the greatest and most formidable that ever was in the world. Five hundred different people, perhaps, who, in different ways, act immediately under the continental congress, and five hundred thousand, perhaps, who act under those five hundred, all feel, in the same manner, a proportionable rise in their own importance. Almost every individual of the governing party in America fills, at present, in his own fancy, a station superior, not only to what he had ever filled before, but to what he had ever expected to fill; and unless some new object of ambition is presented either to him or to his leaders, if he has the ordinary spirit of a man, he will die in defence of that station.
p163.zh: 罗马共和国的盟国在走向罗马共和国的决裂时,承担了保卫国家和扩大帝国的主要负担,要求被接纳为罗马公民的所有特权.遭到拒绝后,社会战争爆发. 在战争期间,罗马将这些特权逐一给予他们中的大部分人,并按他们脱离一般邦联的比例给予. 大不列颠的议会坚持对殖民地征税;他们拒绝被他们没有代表的议会征税. 如果每个殖民地脱离总的邦联,大不列颠就应该允许这样一批代表,这些代表应与其对帝国公共收入的贡献比例相称,因为英国受到同样的税收,并且作为补偿,与国内的同伴一样享有同样的贸易自由;其代表人数随着其贡献比例随后可能增加而增加;将向每个殖民地的领袖们提出一种新的增加重要性的方法,即一个新的和更加令人目眩的雄心壮志的目标。而不是在所谓的殖民地派别的微小奖项中挖苦他们,然后他们可能希望从人们自然能够和幸运的假设中抽取一些大奖,这些奖项有时来自英国政治的大奖项的轮子。 除非这一方法或某种其他方法落空,而且似乎没有比这更明显的是,保持美国领导者的重要性和满足他们的雄心壮志,否则他们不大可能自愿向我们屈服;而且我们应该考虑的是,迫使他们这样做所必须流下的血,就是那些现在的人或我们愿意为我们的公民而流的血。 他们非常软弱,他们自夸,在事物降临的状态下,我们的殖民地很容易被武力征服. 现在管理他们称之为大陆大会的决议的人,此刻感到自己具有某种程度的重要性,也许欧洲最伟大的主体很少感到这种重要性。 从店主、商人和律师那里,他们成为政治家和立法者,受雇为广泛的帝国设计一种新的政府形式,他们自夸地说,这个帝国将会成为,而且确实,它似乎很可能成为世界上最伟大和最强大的帝国之一。五百个不同的人,也许,他们以不同的方式,在大陆大会下立即行动,五十万个,也许,他们在这五百个下行动,都觉得,同样的方式,他们自己的重要性可以按比例上升. 美国执政党的几乎每一个人,目前都以自己的想象,充斥着一个站台的上司,不仅达到他以前所填满的,而且达到他所期望的填充;并且除非有人向他或他的领导人提出一些新的野心目标,如果他有一个人的普通精神,他就会为保卫那个站台而死.

p164.original: It is a remark of the President Heynaut, that we now read with pleasure the account of many little transactions of the Ligue, which, when they happened, were not, perhaps, considered as very important pieces of news. But everyman then, says he, fancied himself of some importance; and the innumerable memoirs which have come down to us from those times, were the greater part of them written by people who took pleasure in recording and magnifying events, in which they flattered themselves they had been considerable actors. How obstinately the city of Paris, upon that occasion, defended itself, what a dreadful famine it supported, rather than submit to the best, and afterwards the most beloved of all the French kings, is well known. The greater part of the citizens, or those who governed the greater part of them, fought in defence of their own importance, which, they foresaw, was to be at an end whenever the ancient government should be re-established. Our colonies, unless they can be induced to consent to a union, are very likely to defend themselves, against the best of all mother countries, as obstinately as the city of Paris did against one of the best of kings.
p164.zh: 海努特总统说,我们现在愉快地阅读了 " 联盟 " 的许多小笔交易的叙述,当这些交易发生时,也许没有被视为非常重要的新闻。 但是,每个人都说,他幻想着自己具有某种重要性;从那些时代下来给我们的无数回忆录,是他们中的大部分是那些乐于记录和放大事件的人写的,他们在其中夸大了自己,他们曾经是相当的演员。巴黎市在那个时刻如何顽固地为自己辩护,它所支持的多么可怕的饥荒,而不是屈从于最优秀的人,后来所有法国国王中最受爱戴的人,是众所周知的.大部分的公民,或者说统治他们大部的人,为了捍卫他们自己的重要性而斗争,他们预见到,只要古代政府应该重建,就应该结束这场斗争. 我们的殖民地,除非可以诱导他们同意联合,否则极有可能保卫自己,对抗所有最优秀的母国,就像巴黎市对最优秀的国王之一所做的那样顽固.

p165.original: The idea of representation was unknown in ancient times. When the people of one state were admitted to the right of citizenship in another, they had no other means of exercising that right, but by coming in a body to vote and deliberate with the people of that other state. The admission of the greater part of the inhabitants of Italy to the privileges of Roman citizens, completely ruined the Roman republic. It was no longer possible to distinguish between who was, and who was not, a Roman citizen. No tribe could know its own members. A rabble of any kind could be introduced into the assemblies of the people, could drive out the real citizens, and decide upon the affairs of the republic, as if they themselves had been such. But though America were to send fifty or sixty new representatives to parliament, the door-keeper of the house of commons could not find any great difficulty in distinguishing between who was and who was not a member. Though the Roman constitution, therefore, was necessarily ruined by the union of Rome with the allied states of Italy, there is not the least probability that the British constitution would be hurt by the union of Great Britain with her colonies. That constitution, on the contrary, would be completed by it, and seems to be imperfect without it. The assembly which deliberates and decides concerning the affairs of every part of the empire, in order to be properly informed, ought certainly to have representatives from every part of it. That this union, however, could be easily effectuated, or that difficulties, and great difficulties, might not occur in the execution, I do not pretend. I have yet heard of none, however, which appear insurmountable. The principal, perhaps, arise, not from the nature of things, but from the prejudices and opinions of the people, both on this and on the other side of the Atlantic.
p165.zh: 代表思想在古代是未知的. 当一个国家的人民被承认在另一个国家拥有公民权时,他们没有其他行使这种权利的手段,只能通过进入一个机构与该另一个国家的人民一起投票和审议。接纳意大利大部分居民享受罗马公民的特权,彻底毁了罗马共和国.已经无法区分谁是、谁是罗马公民。没有一个部落知道自己的成员。任何类型的暴动都可以引入到人民大会中,可以赶走真正的公民,决定共和国的事务,好像他们自己就是那样。 但是,虽然美国要向议会派遣50或60名新代表,但是在区分谁是和谁是非成员方面,公社的门将却找不到任何很大的困难. 虽然罗马宪法因此必然被罗马与意大利的同盟国联合所破坏,但英国宪法不会因为大不列颠与她的殖民地联合而受到损害的概率最小. 相反,这一宪法将会由它完成,而且没有它似乎不完美。讨论和决定帝国每个部分的事务,以便适当了解情况的议会,当然应该有它每个部分的代表。 然而,这种结合是很容易实现的,或者在处决中可能不会出现困难和巨大困难,我不假装。 然而,我还没有听说过任何看来无法克服的问题。主要的,也许,不是源于事物的性质,而是源于人们对大西洋这一边和另一边的偏见和意见。

p166.original: We on this side the water are afraid lest the multitude of American representatives should overturn the balance of the constitution, and increase too much either the influence of the crown on the one hand, or the force of the democracy on the other. But if the number of American representatives were to be in proportion to the produce of American taxation, the number of people to be managed would increase exactly in proportion to the means of managing them, and the means of managing to the number of people to be managed. The monarchical and democratical parts of the constitution would, after the union, stand exactly in the same degree of relative force with regard to one another as they had done before.
p166.zh: 我们这边的水怕美国众多的代表会推翻宪法的平衡,或者增加太多王冠的影响,或者增加民主的力量。 但是,如果美国代表的人数要与美国税收产量成比例,那么所管理的人数就会按照管理手段的准确比例增加,管理手段也要与所管理的人数成正比.宪法的君主制和民主部分在结合之后,彼此之间的相对效力与以前完全相同。

p167.original: The people on the other side of the water are afraid lest their distance from the seat of government might expose them to many oppressions; but their representatives in parliament, of which the number ought from the first to be considerable, would easily be able to protect them from all oppression. The distance could not much weaken the dependency of the representative upon the constituent, and the former would still feel that he owed his seat in parliament, and all the consequence which he derived from it, to the good-will of the latter. It would be the interest of the former, therefore, to cultivate that good-will, by complaining, with all the authority of a member of the legislature, of every outrage which any civil or military officer might be guilty of in those remote parts of the empire. The distance of America from the seat of government, besides, the natives of that country might flatter themselves, with some appearance of reason too, would not be of very long continuance. Such has hitherto been the rapid progress of that country in wealth, population, and improvement, that in the course of little more than a century, perhaps, the produce of the American might exceed that of the British taxation. The seat of the empire would then naturally remove itself to that part of the empire which contributed most to the general defence and support of the whole.
p167.zh: 水的另一边的人民害怕他们远离政府所在地会使他们暴露于许多压迫之下;但是他们在议会中的代表,从第一个数量应该相当大,很容易保护他们免受一切压迫. 这种距离不会大大削弱代表对组成者的依赖,而前者仍然认为,他之所以在议会中占有席位,以及由此而产生的一切后果,都归功于后者的善意。 因此,前者的利益是培养这种善意,在立法机构成员的所有权威下,抱怨任何文职或军官在帝国这些偏远地区可能犯下的任何暴行。 此外,美国与政府所在地的距离,该国原住民可能自以为是,但似乎也有些道理,这不会持续太久。 迄今为止,美国在财富、人口和改善方面的迅速进步,也许在不到一个多世纪的时间里,美国的产品可能超过英国的税收。 然后帝国的所在地自然地 消失在帝国的这个部分 因为它对一般的防御和整个人的支持贡献最大

p168.original: The discovery of America, and that of a passage to the East Indies by the Cape of Good Hope, are the two greatest and most important events recorded in the history of mankind. Their consequences have already been great; but, in the short period of between two and three centuries which has elapsed since these discoveries were made, it is impossible that the whole extent of their consequences can have been seen. What benefits or what misfortunes to mankind may hereafter result from those great events, no human wisdom can foresee. By uniting in some measure the most distant parts of the world, by enabling them to relieve one another's wants, to increase one another's enjoyments, and to encourage one another's industry, their general tendency would seem to be beneficial. To the natives, however, both of the East and West Indies, all the commercial benefits which can have resulted from those events have been sunk and lost in the dreadful misfortunes which they have occasioned. These misfortunes, however, seem to have arisen rather from accident than from any thing in the nature of those events themselves. At the particular time when these discoveries were made, the superiority of force happened to be so great on the side of the Europeans, that they were enabled to commit with impunity every sort of injustice in those remote countries. Hereafter, perhaps, the natives of those countries may grow stronger, or those of Europe may grow weaker; and the inhabitants of all the different quarters of the world may arrive at that equality of courage and force which, by inspiring mutual fear, can alone overawe the injustice of independent nations into some sort of respect for the rights of one another. But nothing seems more likely to establish this equality of force, than that mutual communication of knowledge, and of all sorts of improvements, which an extensive commerce from all countries to all countries naturally, or rather necessarily, carries along with it.
p168.zh: 美国的发现,以及好望角通往东印度群岛的通道的发现,是人类历史上记录的两件最伟大和最重要的事件.其后果已经很严重;但是,在自这些发现以来的两个世纪到三个世纪的短时期内,不可能看到其后果的全部程度。人类未来可能从这些重大事件得到什么好处或什么不幸,人类智慧是无法预见的。 通过在某种程度上统一世界最遥远的地区,通过使它们能够减轻彼此的欲望,增加彼此的享受,鼓励彼此的产业,它们的总的趋势似乎是有益的. 然而,对东印度和西印度群岛的当地人来说,这些事件可能带来的所有商业利益都已沉没,在他们造成的可怕不幸中丧失殆尽。 然而,这些不幸似乎是事故造成的,而不是这些事件本身性质上的任何事物造成的。 在作出这些发现的特定时刻,欧洲人的力量优越性恰好如此之大,以至于他们能够在这些遥远的国家犯下各种不公正行为而不受惩罚。后世,也许这些国家的土著可能变得更加强大,或者欧洲的土著可能变得更加弱小;世界所有不同地区的居民可能实现勇气和力量的平等,而这种平等通过激发相互恐惧,可以单独地夸大独立国家的不公正行为,形成对彼此权利的某种尊重。 但是,最有可能实现这种力量平等之处莫过于相互交流知识和各种改进,而各国对所有国家的广泛商业自然或必然伴随着这种交流。

p169.original: In the mean time, one of the principal effects of those discoveries has been, to raise the mercantile system to a degree of splendour and glory which it could never otherwise have attained to. It is the object of that system to enrich a great nation, rather by trade and manufactures than by the improvement and cultivation of land, rather by the industry of the towns than by that of the country. But in consequence of those discoveries, the commercial towns of Europe, instead of being the manufacturers and carriers for but a very small part of the world (that part of Europe which is washed by the Atlantic ocean, and the countries which lie round the Baltic and Mediterranean seas), have now become the manufacturers for the numerous and thriving cultivators of America, and the carriers, and in some respects the manufacturers too, for almost all the different nations of Asia, Africa, and America. Two new worlds have been opened to their industry, each of them much greater and more extensive than the old one, and the market of one of them growing still greater and greater every day.
p169.zh: 在最短的时间内,这些发现的主要效果之一是将商贸制度提升到它本来不可能达到的辉煌和荣耀的程度。这一制度的目的是通过贸易和制造来丰富一个伟大的国家,而不是通过改良和耕种土地来丰富国家,而是由城镇工业而不是国家工业来丰富国家。 但是,由于这些发现,欧洲的商业城镇不是世界上极少数地区的制造商和载体(被大西洋冲洗的欧洲地区,以及波罗的海和地中海周围的国家),而是现在成为美国众多和兴旺的种植者的制造商,以及载体,在某些方面,也是亚洲、非洲和美国几乎所有不同国家的制造商。 两个新的世界已经向它们的工业开放,它们各自比旧的世界大得多,范围更广,其中之一的市场仍然日复一日地增长。

p170.original: The countries which possess the colonies of America, and which trade directly to the East Indies, enjoy indeed the whole show and splendour of this great commerce. Other countries, however, notwithstanding all the invidious restraints by which it is meant to exclude them, frequently enjoy a greater share of the real benefit of it. The colonies of Spain and Portugal, for example, give more real encouragement to the industry of other countries than to that of Spain and Portugal. In the single article of linen alone, the consumption of those colonies amounts, it is said (but I do not pretend to warrant the quantity ), to more than three millions sterling a-year. But this great consumption is almost entirely supplied by France, Flanders, Holland, and Germany. Spain and Portugal furnish but a small part of it. The capital which supplies the colonies with this great quantity of linen, is annually distributed among, and furnishes a revenue to, the inhabitants of those other countries. The profits of it only are spent in Spain and Portugal, where they help to support the sumptuous profusion of the merchants of Cadiz and Lisbon.
p170.zh: 拥有美洲殖民地,直接与东印度群岛贸易的国家,确实享受了这一伟大商业的全部表现和辉煌。 然而,其他国家尽管受到种种令人反感的限制,却往往享受到更多的实际利益。 例如,西班牙和葡萄牙的殖民地比西班牙和葡萄牙更真正地鼓励其他国家的工业。单是亚麻,这些殖民地的消费就达到了每年300多万英镑(但我不假装需要数量)。 但这种巨大的消费几乎完全由法国,佛兰德,荷兰和德国提供. 西班牙和葡萄牙提供了其中一小部分。向殖民地提供如此大量亚麻的资本每年在这些国家居民之间分配,并向他们提供收入。其利润只在西班牙和葡萄牙使用,他们帮助支持卡迪兹和里斯本商人的丰盛繁殖.

p171.original: Even the regulations by which each nation endeavours to secure to itself the exclusive trade of its own colonies, are frequently more hurtful to the countries in favour of which they are established, than to those against which they are established. The unjust oppression of the industry of other countries falls back, if I may say so, upon the heads of the oppressors, and crushes their industry more than it does that of those other countries. By those regulations, for example, the merchant of Hamburg must send the linen which he destines for the American market to London, and he must bring back from thence the tobacco which he destines for the German market; because he can neither send the one directly to America, nor bring the other directly from thence. By this restraint he is probably obliged to sell the one somewhat cheaper, and to buy the other somewhat dearer, than he otherwise might have done; and his profits are probably somewhat abridged by means of it. In this trade, however, between Hamburg and London, he certainly receives the returns of his capital much more quickly than he could possibly have done in the direct trade to America, even though we should suppose, what is by no means the case, that the payments of America were as punctual as those of London. In the trade, therefore, to which those regulations confine the merchant of Hamburg, his capital can keep in constant employment a much greater quantity of German industry than he possibly could have done in the trade from which he is excluded. Though the one employment, therefore, may to him perhaps be less profitable than the other, it cannot be less advantageous to his country. It is quite otherwise with the employment into which the monopoly naturally attracts, if I may say so, the capital of the London merchant. That employment may, perhaps, be more profitable to him than the greater part of other employments; but on account of the slowness of the returns, it cannot be more advantageous to his country.
p171.zh: 即使每个国家力图确保自己殖民地的专属贸易的条例,往往对建立它们的国家比对建立它们的国家更有害。 对其他国家工业的不公正压迫,如果我可以这样说的话,倒退到压迫者的头上,并且比那些其他国家的工业更加粉碎了它们的工业。 例如,根据这些条例,汉堡的商人必须将他为美国市场所掠夺的亚麻运往伦敦,他必须从那里将他为德国市场所掠夺的烟草运回伦敦;因为他既不能直接将烟草运回美国,也不能直接从那里运回。 由于这种限制,他可能不得不将一个稍便宜一点的出售给另一个稍贵一点的购买人,而他本来可能这样做;他的利润可能因这种手段而略微减少。 然而,在汉堡和伦敦之间的这种贸易中,他肯定比他在美国的直接贸易中可能做到的要快得多,尽管我们不应认为美国付款的及时性与伦敦一样。 因此,在这些条例限制汉堡商人的贸易中,他的资本能够使德国工业持续就业,比他在被排除在外的贸易中可能从事的多得多。 因此,尽管对他而言,一种工作也许比另一种工作获利较少,但对他的国家来说,这种工作不能不有利。 相反,如果我可以说,垄断自然吸引伦敦商人的首都,这种就业是完全相反的。 或许,这种就业对他来说比其他就业的更大部分更有利可图;但是,由于返回的速度缓慢,对于他的国家来说,这种就业再有利不过了。

p172.original: After all the unjust attempts, therefore, of every country in Europe to engross to itself the whole advantage of the trade of its own colonies, no country has yet been able to engross to itself any thing but the expense of supporting in time of peace, and of defending in time of war, the oppressive authority which it assumes over them. The inconveniencies resulting from the possession of its colonies, every country has engrossed to itself completely. The advantages resulting from their trade, it has been obliged to share with many other countries.
p172.zh: 因此,欧洲每个国家在试图将本国殖民地贸易的全部优势为自己攫取一切不公正的企图之后,除了在和平时期支持和在战争时期捍卫它所占据的压迫性权威的费用之外,还没有一个国家能够为自己攫取任何东西。因其殖民地的占有而导致的不便,每个国家都完全陷入了自己的境地. 由于贸易的好处,它不得不与许多其他国家分享。

p173.original: At first sight, no doubt, the monopoly of the great commerce of America naturally seems to be an acquisition of the highest value. To the undiscerning eye of giddy ambition it naturally presents itself, amidst the confused scramble of politics and war, as a very dazzling object to fight for. The dazzling splendour of the object, however, the immense greatness of the commerce, is the very quality which renders the monopoly of it hurtful, or which makes one employment, in its own nature necessarily less advantageous to the country than the greater part of other employments, absorb a much greater proportion of the capital of the country than what would otherwise have gone to it.
p173.zh: 乍一看,毫无疑问,美国大商业的垄断性自然似乎是价值最高的收购. 在政治和战争的混乱中,它自然地呈现出它自己,作为一个令人目眩的物体来为之奋斗。 然而,这个目标令人目眩的光辉,商业的巨大性格,正是它使垄断变得非常有害,或者它使一种就业在本质上必然比其他就业中的大部分对国家更不利,它吸收了该国资本的比例比本来会流向它的比例大得多。

p174.original: The mercantile stock of every country, it has been shown in the second book, naturally seeks, if one may say so, the employment most advantageous to that country. If it is employed in the carrying trade, the country to which it belongs becomes the emporium of the goods of all the countries whose trade that stock carries on. But the owner of that stock necessarily wishes to dispose of as great a part of those goods as he can at home. He thereby saves himself the trouble, risk, and expense of exportation; and he will upon that account be glad to sell them at home, not only for a much smaller price, but with somewhat a smaller profit, than he might expect to make by sending them abroad. He naturally, therefore, endeavours as much as he can to turn his carrying trade into a foreign trade of consumption, If his stock, again, is employed in a foreign trade of consumption, he will, for the same reason, be glad to dispose of, at home, as great a part as he can of the home goods which he collects in order to export to some foreign market, and he will thus endeavour, as much as he can, to turn his foreign trade of consumption into a home trade. The mercantile stock of every country naturally courts in this manner the near, and shuns the distant employment: naturally courts the employment in which the returns are frequent, and shuns that in which they are distant and slow; naturally courts the employment in which it can maintain the greatest quantity of productive labour in the country to which it belongs, or in which its owner resides, and shuns that in which it can maintain there the smallest quantity. It naturally courts the employment which in ordinary cases is most advantageous, and shuns that which in ordinary cases is least advantageous to that country.
p174.zh: 每个国家的商品库存在第二本书中已经显示,如果可以说,它自然寻求对该国最有利的就业。 如果它受雇于载货贸易,它所属的国家就成为其贸易所继续的所有国家的货物的代用品。 但是,该股票的所有人必然希望尽其所能地处置其中一部分货物。 这样,他就可以省去出口的麻烦、风险和开支;他愿意通过这一帐户在国内出售这些物品,不仅价格低得多,而且利润略小一些,比他寄往国外可望达到的利润要少。 因此,他自然会尽力将他的载货贸易转变为对外消费贸易,如果他的股票再次受雇于对外消费贸易,他就会因为同样的原因高兴地在国内处置他为了出口到一些外国市场而收集的家用商品,从而尽力将他的对外消费贸易转变为家用贸易。每个国家的商贸储备都以这种方式自然地法院接近并避开遥远的就业:自然法院裁决返回频繁的就业,并回避那些遥远和缓慢的就业;自然法院裁决在其所属国家或其所有者居住的国家能够维持最大数量生产性劳动力的就业,并回避能够在那里维持最小数量的就业。 它自然会审判在普通案件中最有利的工作,并回避在普通案件中对该国最不利的工作。

p175.original: But if, in any one of those distant employments, which in ordinary cases are less advantageous to the country, the profit should happen to rise somewhat higher than what is sufficient to balance the natural preference which is given to nearer employments, this superiority of profit will draw stock from those nearer employments, till the profits of all return to their proper level. This superiority of profit, however, is a proof that, in the actual circumstances of the society, those distant employments are somewhat understocked in proportion to other employments, and that the stock of the society is not distributed in the properest manner among all the different employments carried on in it. It is a proof that something is either bought cheaper or sold dearer than it ought to be, and that some particular class of citizens is more or less oppressed, either by paying more, or by getting less than what is suitable to that equality which ought to take place, and which naturally does take place, among all the different classes of them. Though the same capital never will maintain the same quantity of productive labour in a distant as in a near employment, yet a distant employment maybe as necessary for the welfare of the society as a near one; the goods which the distant employment deals in being necessary, perhaps, for carrying on many of the nearer employments. But if the profits of those who deal in such goods are above their proper level, those goods will be sold dearer than they ought to be, or somewhat above their natural price, and all those engaged in the nearer employments will be more or less oppressed by this high price. Their interest, therefore, in this case, requires, that some stock should be withdrawn from those nearer employments, and turned towards that distant one, in order to reduce its profits to their proper level, and the price of the goods which it deals in to their natural price. In this extraordinary case, the public interest requires that some stock should be withdrawn from those employments which, in ordinary cases, are more advantageous, and turned towards one which, in ordinary cases, is less advantageous to the public; and, in this extraordinary case, the natural interests and inclinations of men coincide as exactly with the public interests as in all other ordinary cases, and lead them to withdraw stock from the near, and to turn it towards the distant employments.
p175.zh: 但是,如果在任何一种较远的就业中,在一般情况下对本国不利,利润的上升幅度应略高于对较近就业的自然偏好加以平衡的程度,那么这种利润的优越性将从较近就业者手中提取,直到所有利润都恢复到适当的水平。 然而,利润的这种优越性证明,在社会的实际状况下,这些遥远的就业与其他就业的比例有些不足,而且社会存量没有以最适当的方式在它从事的所有不同就业中分配。 这证明,有些东西要么买得起,要么卖得比应该买的要便宜,要么卖得更贵,而且某些特定阶层的公民或多或少地受到压迫,或者得到的比应该实现的平等更低,而这种平等是在所有阶层中自然发生的。 虽然同一资本在遥远的就业机会中永远不会维持与在接近的就业机会中相同的生产性劳动力数量,但遥远的就业机会或许是社会福祉所必要的;遥远的就业机会所交易的商品或许是从事许多较接近的就业机会所必需的。 但是,如果这些货物交易者的利润高于其适当水平,这些货物就会被卖得比他们应该卖得更贵,或者略高于其自然价格,而且所有从事较接近就业的人都会受到这种高价的多少压迫。 因此,在这种情况下,它们的利益要求从那些较接近就业的人手中撤出一些股票,然后转向遥远的股票,以便将其利润降低到适当的水平,并将所交易货物的价格降低到其自然价格。 在这种特殊情况下,公共利益要求从那些在普通情况下更有利、转而对公众更不利的工作中撤出一些股票;在这种特殊情况下,男子的自然利益和倾向与所有其他普通情况下的公共利益完全一致,并导致他们从近处撤出股票,转向遥远的工作。

p176.original: It is thus that the private interests and passions of individuals naturally dispose them to turn their stock towards the employments which in ordinary cases, are most advantageous to the society. But if from this natural preference they should turn too much of it towards those employments, the fall of profit in them, and the rise of it in all others, immediately dispose them to alter this faulty distribution. Without any intervention of law, therefore, the private interests and passions of men naturally lead them to divide and distribute the stock of every society among all the different employments carried on in it; as nearly as possible in the proportion which is most agreeable to the interest of the whole society.
p176.zh: 因此,个人的私人利益和热情自然决定了他们把财富转向在普通情况下对社会最有利的就业。 但是,如果从这种自然的偏好来看,他们应该把太多的精力转向这些就业,那么利润的下降,以及所有其他就业的上升,就立即决定改变这种错误的分布。 因此,在没有任何法律干预的情况下,男子的私人利益和热情自然导致他们把每个社会的资产分割和分配在它从事的所有不同职业中;尽可能按照最符合整个社会利益的比例分配。

p177.original: All the different regulations of the mercantile system necessarily derange more or less this natural and most advantageous distribution of stock. But those which concern the trade to America and the East Indies derange it, perhaps, more than any other; because the trade to those two great continents absorbs a greater quantity of stock than any two other branches of trade. The regulations, however, by which this derangement is effected in those two different branches of trade, are not altogether the same.
